definition_zh: 内在本质的；本身价值的；内在动机的；内禀的；内部的（肌肉）；内蕴的（曲率）；本征的（半导体）；内生的（增长）
definition_en: belonging to the inner nature of a thing and measured without reference to anything outside it
core_image: 拍卖台上摆着一幅无人出价的旧素描，鉴定师却只说它的价值不在标签上
scene: 拍卖行把一幅无人问津的旧素描摆上台面，鉴定师却说它的分量不在价签上。The old sketch has an intrinsic worth that no auction price can measure.
sceneCN: 这里指事物自身所具有、不由外界定价的价值（第 2 个义项：不依赖外部评价的内在价值）；句意为这幅旧素描有一种拍卖价量不出的内在价值。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「本质上；就其自身而言」
由该形容词的词干加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「内在性；固有性」，多用于哲学
由对应的拉丁「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的；外来的」，是与目标词成对的反义对照词

senses.title: Belonging to a thing's own nature
senses.definition: forming part of what something is in itself, independent of how others regard it
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物自身之所是，与别人如何看待它无关
senses.example: Curiosity seems intrinsic to the human mind.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心似乎是人心本身固有的。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'on the inside', so a quality located within a thing's own nature is intrinsic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「在内侧」，因此位于事物自身本性之中的性质就是内在的。

senses.title: Worth that is not set by a market
senses.definition: value that a thing has in itself, apart from price, usefulness or what buyers will pay
senses.definitionCN: 事物自身即有的价值，与价格、用途或买家的出价无关
senses.example: Philosophers debate whether art has intrinsic value.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论艺术是否具有内在价值。
senses.why: If worth is inside the thing, then an outside price can measure it only indirectly, if at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果价值在事物内部，那么外部价格至多只能间接地量到它。

senses.title: Drive that comes from within
senses.definition: motivation arising from interest or enjoyment rather than from external reward or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 由兴趣或乐趣产生的动机，而非来自外部奖励或压力
senses.example: Intrinsic motivation keeps volunteers coming back.
senses.exampleCN: 内在动机让志愿者一再回来。
senses.why: The source of the drive sits inside the person, which is exactly what the word locates inside.
senses.whyCN: 动力的源头在人的内部，而这正是这个词所定位的「内侧」。

senses.title: A property independent of amount
senses.titleCN: 与数量多少无关的性质
senses.definition: in physics, a property of a material that does not change when the sample size changes
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中不随样品大小改变的材料性质
senses.example: Density is intrinsic; mass is not.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是内禀性质，质量不是。
senses.why: A property that stays the same whether you take a gram or a tonne belongs to the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 无论取一克还是一吨都不变的性质，属于物质自身。

senses.title: Muscles lying inside an organ
senses.definition: in anatomy, said of muscles whose origin and insertion lie within the structure they move
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中起止点都位于其所运动结构内部的肌肉
senses.example: The intrinsic muscles of the hand control the fingers finely.
senses.exampleCN: 手部内在肌精细地控制手指。
senses.why: Anatomy contrasts muscles inside an organ with ones that enter it from outside.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把器官内部的肌肉与从外部伸入的肌肉相对照。

senses.title: Curvature measurable from inside
senses.definition: in geometry, a curvature determined by measurements within the surface itself, without embedding it in a larger space
senses.definitionCN: 几何中只靠曲面内部的测量即可确定的曲率，无需把曲面嵌入更大空间
senses.example: Intrinsic curvature can be detected by triangles on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 内蕴曲率可以通过曲面上的三角形测出。
senses.why: If the measurement needs nothing outside, the property is literally intrinsic to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 若测量不需要任何外部条件，该性质就字面地内在于曲面之中。

senses.title: Pure, undoped material
senses.definition: in electronics, said of a semiconductor whose behaviour comes from its own pure crystal, with no added impurities
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中行为来自纯净晶体本身、未添加杂质的半导体
senses.example: Intrinsic silicon conducts far less than doped silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 本征硅的导电性远低于掺杂硅。
senses.why: Its electrical behaviour is a property of the pure material, not of anything added from outside.
senses.whyCN: 它的电学行为来自纯净材料本身，而不是外部添加物。

senses.title: Growth generated from inside
senses.definition: in economics, growth produced by internal factors such as knowledge and investment in people, not by outside shocks
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中由知识、对人的投资等内部因素产生的增长，而非外部冲击带来
senses.example: Intrinsic growth models stress education over foreign aid.
senses.exampleCN: 内生增长模型强调教育胜过外国援助。
senses.why: The model looks for the causes of growth inside the economy rather than outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这类模型在经济体内部寻找增长原因，而不是在外部寻找。

intro.en: Intrinsic comes from Late Latin intrinsecus 'inwardly, on the inside', built on intra 'within' and secus 'alongside'. French intrinsèque carried it into English in the seventeenth century, paired with extrinsic. The direct source is clear; the earlier makeup of secus is still debated.
intro.cn: intrinsic 来自晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「向内的、在内侧的」，由 intra「在内」与 secus「沿着、旁边」构成。法语 intrinsèque 在十七世纪把它带进英语，并与 extrinsic 成对。直接来源清楚；更早的 secus 构成仍有争议。

items.en: Intra meant within or inside, and it still appears in English words such as intravenous.
items.cn: intra 意为在……之内，至今出现在 intravenous 等英语词中。

items.en: Secus meant alongside or beside; its further origin is disputed, so the internal makeup of the compound is not certain.
items.cn: secus 意为沿着、在旁边；它更早的来源有争议，因此这个复合词的内部构成并非确证。

items.en: The adverb meant inward or on the inside, and it described what belongs to a thing from within.
items.cn: 这个副词意为向内、在内侧，描述从内部属于某物的东西。

items.en: Its partner meant from outside, and the pair intrinsic and extrinsic still divide inner nature from external circumstance.
items.cn: 与之配对的形式意为「从外部」，如今「内在」与「外在」这一对仍用于区分本性与外部环境。

items.en: English took intrinsic through French for qualities belonging to a thing itself, especially in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个词，用于属于事物自身的性质，尤其在哲学与神学中。

items.en: Physics, anatomy, geometry and economics each gave the word a measured meaning where 'inside' can be tested.
items.cn: 物理学、解剖学、几何学与经济学各自给这个词一个可检验的「内部」含义。

note.en: The first group is the same word family with its opposite; the second group holds near synonyms that locate qualities differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族及其对立词；第二组是同样描述性质归属、但定位方式不同的近义词。

entries.definition: By its own nature, without reference to outside standards; it marks the source of value.
entries.definitionCN: 就其自身本性而言，不参照外部标准；标出价值的来源。

entries.definition: The quality of belonging to a thing's inner nature; a rare philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物内在本性的性质；少见的哲学名词。

entries.definition: Coming from outside, such as reward, price or circumstance; the exact opposite partner.
entries.definitionCN: 来自外部的东西，如奖励、价格或环境；正是与之相对的另一半。

entries.definition: An older variant spelling of the same adjective, now mostly replaced by the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较早异体拼法，如今多被较短的形取代。

entries.definition: Stuck to a subject so that it cannot be removed; it stresses attachment, while the target word stresses inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于主体而无法去除；强调「附着」，而目标词强调「内在本质」。

entries.definition: Present from birth; it marks a starting point in time rather than a location inside a nature.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有；标出时间上的起点，而非本性内部的位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be itself; stronger than a mere inner quality.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为自身；比单纯「内在性质」更强。

entries.definition: Designed into a product; the everyday word for what is installed rather than grown from within.
entries.definitionCN: 设计进产品里的；是日常说法，指装进去而非从内部长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'within': intrinsic value is the value inside the thing, not on the price tag.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在内」：内在价值是事物里面的价值，不在价签上。

normal.en: The family runs intrinsically, intrinsicality and the paired opposite extrinsic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本质上、内在性，以及与它成对的外在的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark value and drive: intrinsic value, intrinsic motivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出价值与动力：内在价值、内在动机。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: intrinsic property, intrinsic semiconductor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：内禀性质、本征半导体。

normal.en: Its opposite is extrinsic, which puts the source outside the thing.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 extrinsic，把来源放在事物外部。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose shine comes from its own metal, not the light in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的光泽来自它自己的金属，而不是房间里的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who trains because the running itself feels good.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者训练，因为跑这件事本身让他舒服。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose warmth comes from its stones, not from a heater.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的暖意来自石头本身，而不是暖气。

examples.en: The painting's intrinsic value lies in its brushwork, not its price.
examples.cn: 这幅画的内在价值在笔法，而不在价格。

examples.en: Children learn faster when motivation is intrinsic.
examples.cn: 当动机来自内心时，孩子学得更快。

examples.en: Conductivity is an intrinsic property of the pure crystal.
examples.cn: 导电性是纯晶体的内禀性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印吹壳」——印在壳子最里面那一层，从外看不见，就是内在的

root: 拉丁 intra「在内」+ secus「沿着、旁边」→ 晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「内侧的」→ 法语 intrinsèque → 英语 intrinsic；与 extrinsecus「外在的」成对。secus 的更早来源尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality inside its owner: in a nature, a value, a motive, a material property, an organ, a surface, a crystal or an economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种性质放在所有者内部：放在本性里、价值里、动机里、材料性质里、器官里、曲面里、晶体里，或经济体里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality that lives inside a thing, so outside measures can only approach it.
core.cn: 核心意象：住在事物内部的一种性质，外部量度只能靠近它。

branches.en: THE NATURE SENSE: what a thing is in itself, apart from outside opinion.
branches.cn: 本性义：某物自身之所是，与外部看法无关。

branches.en: THE VALUED AND MOTIVATED SIDE: worth not set by a market, and interest that needs no reward.
branches.cn: 价值与动力一面：不由市场定价的价值，以及无需奖励的兴趣。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: properties unchanged by sample size, and the behaviour of a pure crystal.
branches.cn: 材料一面：不随样品大小改变的性质，以及纯晶体自身的行为。

branches.en: THE ANATOMICAL SIDE: muscles whose ends both lie inside the organ they move.
branches.cn: 解剖一面：两端都在所运动器官内部的肌肉。

branches.en: THE SELF-CONTAINED SIDE: curvature measured within a surface, and growth generated inside an economy.
branches.cn: 自足一面：在曲面内部测得的曲率，以及经济体内部产生的增长。

intro.en: Intrinsic is a Latin adverb turned adjective: intra 'within' plus secus 'alongside', with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: intrinsic 是由拉丁副词转成的形容词：intra「在内」加 secus「沿着」，再加形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Intra plus secus gives the adverb intrinsecus 'inwardly'; the adjective form, through French, is intrinsèque, taken into English as intrinsic.
latinIntro.cn: intra 加 secus 得出副词 intrinsecus「向内」；其形容词形式经法语作 intrinsèque，进入英语成为 intrinsic。

items.example: The prefix locates the quality inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把性质定位在内部。

items.example: Its earlier origin is disputed, so the compound is not fully certain.
items.exampleCN: 它更早的来源有争议，因此该复合词并非完全确证。

items.example: The adverb is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The counterpart gives the paired opposite in English.
items.exampleCN: 配对形式给出英语中的反义对照词。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把副词变成形容词。

items.example: English added measurable technical senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了可量度的技术义。

items.example: The ending gives the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the inner quality in philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在哲学中命名「内在性」。

items.example: The longer form is now archaic.
items.exampleCN: 较长的形式如今已属古旧。

items.example: The opposite partner appears in the same technical fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个对立词出现在同一批技术领域。

由该形容词词干加性质名词后缀构成，义为「内在性」

definition_zh: 介绍；引进；提出；开始
definition_en: to tell people someone's name, to bring something in for the first time, or to begin something
core_image: 一个人牵着另一个人的手，把他领进一间坐满陌生人的屋子
scene: 晚宴开始时，主人走到客人身边，把他们两两凑在一起说名字。They introduced the new system last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 introduce 是「引进、推行」（第 2 个义项：把新事物带入使用），句意为他们去年春天引进了这套新系统。画面里的物件：晚宴长桌、香槟杯、贴着新标签的控制台。

pos.zh: 动词：介绍；引进；提出；作为……的开头

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -tion 构成，义为「介绍；引进；前言」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的；入门的」
由本词截短构成，义为「引言；开场」
同出 duc- 词根，义为「教育的」

senses.title: Make two people known
senses.definition: to tell two people each other's names so that they can begin to know each other
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人的名字，使他们可以开始相识
senses.example: Let me introduce my sister before we sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 坐下之前让我介绍一下我妹妹。
senses.why: Latin ducere means to lead; intro- means inward. To introduce is to lead someone in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」，introduce 就是把人领进来。

senses.title: Bring something in
senses.definition: to bring a new thing, idea, or rule into use for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 首次把新事物、新想法或新规定投入使用
senses.example: The school introduced a later start for older pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为高年级学生推出了更晚的到校时间。
senses.why: The leading-in picture suits ideas too: new rules are walked into a system.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像也适用于想法：新规定被领进一个体系。

senses.title: Become familiar with
senses.definition: to cause someone to experience or learn about something for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人第一次接触或了解某事物
senses.example: Her aunt introduced her to jazz when she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁时，姑母带她第一次接触爵士乐。
senses.why: Here the person is led into a subject as if into a room.
senses.whyCN: 这里人是被领进一门学问，就像被领进一间屋子。

senses.title: Begin a piece
senses.definition: to begin a speech, book, or programme with something
senses.definitionCN: 用某内容作为演讲、书籍或节目的开头
senses.example: The chair introduced the meeting with two minutes of thanks.
senses.exampleCN: 主席用两分钟致谢作为会议的开场。
senses.why: Opening a meeting is leading the audience in, so the same verb serves.
senses.whyCN: 会议开场就是把听众领进来，所以还是用同一个动词。

intro.en: Introduce joins Latin intro- "inward" and ducere "to lead": to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduce 把拉丁语 intro-「向内」与 ducere「引导」结合：把人领进来。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or draw along.
items.cn: ducere 意为带领或牵引。

items.en: Introducere meant to lead a person or thing inside.
items.cn: introducere 意为把人或物领进去。

items.en: French introduire kept the ceremonial sense of bringing someone in.
items.cn: 法语 introduire 保留了把人带进来的礼仪义。

items.en: English used introduce for presenting a person at court or at home.
items.cn: 英语用 introduce 指在宫廷或家中引见某人。

items.en: Industry and law added the sense of putting a new thing into use.
items.cn: 工业与法律又添上「把新事物投入使用」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duce leading root; the near-meaning group holds other words for presenting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duce「引导」词根；近义组收其他表示「推出」的词。

entries.definition: The act or the opening section that results.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「介绍；引言」。

entries.definition: To lead something back or make it smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「减少」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To lead something forward into being.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「生产」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To show or hand over something formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「呈现；呈交」，更正式。

entries.definition: To start using something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「引入」，偏口语。

entries.definition: To start a product or campaign publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「推出；发起」，强调公开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand leading another person indoors.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一只手把别人领进屋里」的画面。

normal.en: intro- inward plus duc lead equals lead in.
normal.cn: intro-「向内」加 duc「引导」等于「领进来」。

normal.en: The same duc root appears in reduce, produce, and conduct.
normal.cn: 同一个 duc 词根出现在 reduce、produce、conduct 里。

normal.en: Introduce yourself is the shortest formal speech you will give.
normal.cn: introduce yourself 是你要讲的最短的正式发言。

normal.en: Schools introduce rules the way hosts introduce guests.
normal.cn: 学校推行规定，就像主人介绍客人。

normal.en: Her aunt introduced her to jazz: led her into a room of sound.
normal.cn: 姑母带她认识爵士：把她领进一间装满声音的屋子。

abstract.en: To introduce is to open a door and stand aside.
abstract.cn: 介绍就是打开一扇门，然后退到一边。

abstract.en: New ideas also need someone to walk them in.
abstract.cn: 新想法也需要有人牵着走进去。

abstract.en: The word is a handshake turned into grammar.
abstract.cn: 这个词是把一次握手写成了语法。

examples.en: She introduced me to her old teacher at the gate.
examples.cn: 她在门口把我介绍给了她的老师。

examples.en: The company introduced a shorter working week.
examples.cn: 公司推行了更短的工作周。

examples.en: He introduced his talk with a story about his father.
examples.cn: 他用一个关于父亲的故事开了讲座的头。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duce（引导）——把人领进门

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introducere「领进去」→ 古法语 introduire → 英语 introduce。同族有 introduction、introductory、produce。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: make people known, bring something new in, lead someone into a subject, and open a piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、带人入门，以及作为开场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand leading another person through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着另一个人穿过门口。

branches.en: THE NAMES: two strangers given to each other.
branches.cn: 名字这条线：两个陌生人被交给彼此。

branches.en: THE RULE: a new practice led into a system.
branches.cn: 规定这条线：新做法被领进一个体系。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a young listener led into jazz.
branches.cn: 唱片这条线：年轻听者被领进爵士。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: an opening line that leads the audience in.
branches.cn: 讲台这条线：把听众领进来的开场白。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses bring someone into a place they did not know.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把某人带进他原本不认识的地方。

intro.en: Introduce is intro- "inward" plus the root duc- "lead" with the verb ending.
intro.cn: introduce 是 intro-「向内」加词根 duc-「引导」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere、introducere 与分词 introductus 均有记载。

definition_zh: 介绍；引进；引言；入门
definition_en: the act of making people known or bringing something in, or the opening part of a book or talk
core_image: 书的正文之前，有一页写着短短几段，把你领进门
scene: 新同事被带到办公区，组长领着他在每张桌前停下说一句。The book's introduction explains why the author began.
sceneCN: 这里 introduction 是「引言、前言」（第 4 个义项：书或讲话的开头部分），句意为这本书的引言说明了作者为何动笔。画面里的物件：新同事、工位、书的扉页。

pos.zh: 名词：介绍；引进；引言；入门介绍

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「介绍；引进」
由 introduce 加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的」
截短形式，义为「开场；引言」

senses.title: Making people known
senses.definition: the act of telling two people each other's names so that they can meet
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人名字使他们得以相识的行为
senses.example: A quiet introduction at the door saved them both embarrassment.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一句轻轻的介绍替两人都免了尴尬。
senses.why: The Latin action noun treats the handshake as a deed with a name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的动作名词把这次握手当成一件有名字的事。

senses.title: Bringing something in
senses.definition: the act of putting a new thing, rule, or idea into use
senses.definitionCN: 把新事物、规定或想法投入使用的行为
senses.example: The introduction of the railway changed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路的引进改变了整个山谷。
senses.why: The same leading-in image applies to machines and policies.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像同样用于机器与政策。

senses.title: A first course
senses.definition: a book or course that teaches the basics of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 讲解某学科基础知识的一本书或一门课
senses.example: This little grammar is a gentle introduction to Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 这本薄薄的语法书是拉丁语的温和入门。
senses.why: A beginner is led in, so the teaching material takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 初学者是被领进去的，于是入门教材也叫这个名字。

senses.title: The opening part
senses.definition: the first section of a book, speech, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、演讲或乐曲的最初部分
senses.example: Read the introduction before you judge the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 先读引言，再评判论证。
senses.why: The opening leads the reader in, exactly what the Latin verb described.
senses.whyCN: 开头把读者领进去，正是那个拉丁动词所描述的。

intro.en: Introduction is the Latin noun on introducere, to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduction 是建立在 introducere（把人领进来）上的拉丁语名词。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead; intro- meant inward.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」。

items.en: Introductio named the act of bringing someone or something in.
items.cn: introductio 指把人或物带进来的行为。

items.en: French kept the noun for a formal presentation of persons.
items.cn: 法语保留了这个名词，指对人的正式引见。

items.en: Printing gave it the sense of the opening pages of a book.
items.cn: 印刷术给了它「书的开篇」义。

items.en: Modern usage adds the introduction of machines and reforms.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上机器与改革的引进。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duct- leading stem; the near-meaning group holds other opening words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duct-「引导」词干；近义组收其他「开头」词。

entries.definition: The verb of leading someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「介绍；引进」。

entries.definition: The adjective for an opening section.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「引导性的」。

entries.definition: The making of goods or a show.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「生产；制作」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short note before the main text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「序言」，作者自述写作缘由。

entries.definition: An opening note often written by someone else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「前言」，多由他人撰写。

entries.definition: A general summary before the details.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「概述」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as the doorway into a book or a group.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它当作一本书或一群人的门口。

normal.en: Introduce is the act; introduction is the act turned into a thing.
normal.cn: introduce 是动作，introduction 是被做成东西的动作。

normal.en: An introduction to economics leads you into the subject.
normal.cn: an introduction to economics 把你领进这门学科。

normal.en: Letters of introduction once opened doors in a new city.
normal.cn: 介绍信曾在陌生城市替你开门。

normal.en: The introduction of the railway is the same word used for machines.
normal.cn: the introduction of the railway 是同词用于机器。

normal.en: Skip the introduction and you may miss why the book exists.
normal.cn: 跳过引言可能就错过了这本书存在的理由。

abstract.en: An introduction is a corridor, not a room.
abstract.cn: 引言是走廊，不是房间。

abstract.en: Every introduction asks you to trust before you know.
abstract.cn: 每次介绍都在你了解之前先请你信任。

abstract.en: A good introduction hands you a lamp, not a map.
abstract.cn: 好的引言递给你一盏灯，而不是一张地图。

examples.en: His introduction to her was made by a mutual friend.
examples.cn: 他是通过一位共同的朋友认识她的。

examples.en: The introduction of parking fees angered local shops.
examples.cn: 停车费的引入让本地商铺不满。

examples.en: She wrote a short introduction to the second edition.
examples.cn: 她为第二版写了一篇简短的引言。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duct（引导）+ ion——把人领进来的那段

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introductio「引见」→ 古法语 → 英语 introduction。同族有 introduce、introductory、intro。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: making people known, bringing something new in, a beginner's course, and an opening section.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、入门课程，以及开篇部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few short pages standing before the main text like a doorman.
core.cn: 核心意象：正文之前几页短文，像一个门房站在那里。

branches.en: THE HANDSHAKE: two people given each other's names.
branches.cn: 握手这条线：两个人被互相报出名字。

branches.en: THE RAILWAY: a new thing led into daily life.
branches.cn: 铁路这条线：新事物被领进日常生活。

branches.en: THE TEXTBOOK: a gentle first course.
branches.cn: 课本这条线：温和的第一课。

branches.en: THE PREFACE: the opening that explains the whole.
branches.cn: 序言这条线：解释全书的开头。

branches.en: THE LINK: both stand at a door and say what comes next.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都站在门口，说明接下来是什么。

intro.en: Introduction is intro- plus the root duct- "lead" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: introduction 由 intro- 加词根 duct-「引导」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin introductio and the participle introductus are recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 introductio 与分词 introductus 都是记载形式。

items.example: It marks the direction of entry.
The root also appears in conduct and product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 conduct 与 product。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
It builds the abstract noun.
The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。

items.example: It forms introductory.
It builds preface, said beforehand.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 preface，意为先说在前。

items.example: It builds foreword, the word in front.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 foreword，即前面的文字。

definition_zh: 侵略；侵入；侵扰；侵犯
definition_en: to enter a country or place by force, or to enter somewhere in large numbers where one is not wanted
core_image: 军队越过界碑，旗帜插进对方的土地
scene: 海面上排开许多小船，天未亮就往沙滩方向划来。Tourists invade the small town every August.
sceneCN: 这里 invade 是「涌入、侵扰」（第 2 个义项：大批进入不受欢迎的地方），句意为每年八月游客涌入这座小镇。画面里的物件：小船、沙滩、界碑。

pos.zh: 动词：侵略；侵入；侵扰；侵犯

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -sion 构成，义为「侵略；侵扰」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「入侵者」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；扩散性的」
同一词根 vadere 构成，义为「逃避」

senses.title: Enter by force
senses.definition: to enter a country or region with armed force in order to conquer it
senses.definitionCN: 以武力进入一国或地区以图征服
senses.example: The army invaded the province at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时入侵了那个省。
senses.why: Latin vadere means to go; in- means into, so the word is simply to go in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vadere 意为「走」，in- 意为「进入」，所以本义就是「走进去」。

senses.title: Arrive in crowds
senses.definition: to enter a place in large numbers, often where people do not welcome it
senses.definitionCN: 大批进入某地，且往往不受欢迎
senses.example: Fans invaded the field in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一分钟球迷涌进了球场。
senses.why: The force of the verb softened into sheer numbers.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的力量感弱化成了「人多」。

senses.title: Trespass on rights or privacy
senses.definition: to intrude on someone's privacy, rights, or personal space
senses.definitionCN: 侵入他人的隐私、权利或个人空间
senses.example: Constant calls invaded what was left of her evening.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的电话侵占了她仅剩的夜晚。
senses.why: Borders can be personal, so invasion moves from land to rights.
senses.whyCN: 界线也可以是个人的，于是「入侵」从土地移到权利。

senses.title: Spread where unwanted
senses.definition: to spread through a body, an environment, or a market where it does harm
senses.definitionCN: 在身体、环境或市场中扩散并造成损害
senses.example: A weed from Asia invaded the riverbanks.
senses.exampleCN: 一种来自亚洲的杂草侵占了河岸。
senses.why: Plants and cells obey the same picture: going where they were not invited.
senses.whyCN: 植物与细胞遵循同一图像：去到自己没被邀请的地方。

intro.en: Invade comes from Latin invadere, to go into, from in- "into" and vadere "to go".
intro.cn: invade 来自拉丁语 invadere「走进去」，由 in-「进入」与 vadere「走」构成。

items.en: Vadere meant to go or to walk forward.
items.cn: vadere 意为行走或向前走。

items.en: Invadere meant to go in, especially with force.
items.cn: invadere 意为走进去，尤指强行进入。

items.en: The noun invasio named a hostile entry.
items.cn: 名词 invasio 指敌意的进入。

items.en: French envahir carried the military sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 envahir 把军事义带入英语。

items.en: The word came to cover crowds, privacy, and disease.
items.cn: 这个词后来覆盖了人群、隐私与疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vade going root; the near-meaning group holds other words for breaking in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vade「走」词根；近义组收其他表示「闯入」的词。

entries.definition: The act or event of invading.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「侵略；入侵」。

entries.definition: To get away from something by dodging.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「逃避」，同出 vadere。

entries.definition: An armed or unwelcome intruder.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「入侵者」。

entries.definition: To enter where one is not welcome or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「闯入」，更强调冒犯。

entries.definition: To take and hold a place by force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「占领」，强调控制而非进入。

entries.definition: A short sudden attack on a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「突袭」，时间短。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a border crossed without permission.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一条界线被人不经允许踩过」的画面。

normal.en: in- into plus vadere go equals go into, uninvited.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 vadere「走」等于未经邀请地走进去。

normal.en: The same going root is inside evade, to go away from trouble.
normal.cn: 同一个「走」的词根藏在 evade 里，那是往麻烦外走。

normal.en: Tourists can invade a town without a single soldier.
normal.cn: 不用一个兵，游客也能侵占一座小镇。

normal.en: Privacy can be invaded by a phone call.
normal.cn: 隐私可以被一通电话侵占。

normal.en: Add -sion and invasion is the event, not the act.
normal.cn: 加 -sion 成 invasion，指那个事件。

abstract.en: To invade is to treat a boundary as a suggestion.
abstract.cn: 入侵是把一条界线当成建议。

abstract.en: Weeds and armies move in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 杂草和军队朝同一个方向推进。

abstract.en: Every invasion begins with a step someone thought was allowed.
abstract.cn: 每次入侵都始于某个自认为被允许的脚步。

examples.en: Neighbours invaded the garden with their footballs every weekend.
examples.cn: 每到周末，邻家孩子就带着足球闯进花园。

examples.en: The company invaded a market long held by two rivals.
examples.cn: 这家公司打入了一个长期由两家对手占据的市场。

examples.en: Reporters must be careful not to invade private grief.
examples.cn: 记者必须小心，别去侵扰别人的私人之痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ vade（走）——径直走进去

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「强行走入」→ invasio「入侵」→ 古法语 envahir → 英语 invade。同族有 invasion、invader、evade。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: armed entry, crowds arriving, trespass on privacy, and harmful spread.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：武力进入、人群涌入、侵犯隐私，以及有害的蔓延。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots stepping across a boundary stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子踩过一块界石。

branches.en: THE ARMY: armed entry across a national border.
branches.cn: 军队这条线：越过国界的武装进入。

branches.en: THE STADIUM: crowds pouring over the rail.
branches.cn: 球场这条线：人群翻过栏杆涌入。

branches.en: THE PHONE: a call that takes a private evening.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：吞掉私人夜晚的来电。

branches.en: THE WEED: a plant colonising a riverbank.
branches.cn: 杂草这条线：占据河岸的植物。

branches.en: THE LINK: both take ground that belonged to others.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都占有了别人的地方。

intro.en: Invade is in- "into" plus the Latin root vad- "go" with a verb ending.
intro.cn: invade 是 in-「进入」加拉丁词根 vad-「走」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere and invadere are recorded; the family also gives English evade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 与 invadere 均有记载，这一族也给英语带来 evade。

items.example: It marks the direction of travel.
The root also lives in evade and pervasive.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 evade 与 pervasive。

items.example: The verb is the base of the root.
The verb is the direct source.
It forms invasion.
It forms invader.
It forms invasive.
It forms evade, to go out of reach.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 evade，意为走出够得着的范围。

definition_zh: 入侵；侵略；侵犯；蜂拥而入
definition_en: the act of an army or a large number of people entering a place by force, or of something harmful spreading in
core_image: 一支队伍踏过界碑，潮水一样涌进别人的院墙
scene: 深夜的海岸线上，探照灯扫过浅滩，士兵从登陆艇上跳进水里。The islanders still tell stories of the invasion.
sceneCN: 这里 invasion 是「入侵」（第 1 个义项：武力进入他国领土），句意为岛民至今仍在讲那次入侵的故事。画面里的物件：探照灯、登陆艇、浅滩。

pos.zh: 名词：入侵；侵略；侵犯；大量涌入

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -sion 加 -de，义为「入侵；侵犯」
由本词词根加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；侵袭性的」
由 invade 加 -er 构成，义为「入侵者」
同带 -sion 尾的形近词，义为「逃避；回避」

senses.title: Army crossing a border
senses.definition: the act of an army entering a country with force in order to take control of it
senses.definitionCN: 军队武力进入他国、企图控制该国的行为
senses.example: The invasion began before dawn and cut the capital off within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵在黎明前开始，一天之内就切断了首都与外界的联系。
senses.why: Latin invadere meant "to go into", built from in- plus vadere, "to go".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invadere 意为「走进去」，由 in- 加 vadere「走」构成。

senses.title: Taking something over
senses.definition: the unwanted entry of a rival power into the affairs or land of another state
senses.definitionCN: 敌对势力不受欢迎地进入他国的事务或领土
senses.example: The treaty promised aid to any member facing an invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺援助任何遭遇侵占的成员国。
senses.why: Once "go into" gained a hostile tone, the noun naturally meant a hostile entry.
senses.whyCN: 「走进去」一旦带上敌意，名词自然就指敌意的进入。

senses.title: Privacy broken into
senses.definition: an unwanted and unlawful entry into someone else's private life or space
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意且不合法地进入他人的私生活或私人空间
senses.example: Reading her letters felt like an invasion of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 看她的信件感觉像是对隐私的侵犯。
senses.why: English extended the military noun to the borders of the self rather than of the state.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个军事名词从国家的边界挪到了个人的边界。

senses.title: A crowd or a plague
senses.definition: a large number of people or things arriving or spreading where they are not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人或事物不受欢迎地到来或蔓延
senses.example: The town is bracing for an invasion of holidaymakers in July.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇正在为七月的度假人群大批涌入做准备。
senses.why: The metaphor of a flood is old: what pours in without being asked counts as an invasion.
senses.whyCN: 「洪水」的比喻很古老：不请自来涌进来的东西都算入侵。

intro.en: Invasion comes straight from Latin invasio, a noun of "going in" onto someone else's ground.
intro.cn: invasion 直接来自拉丁语 invasio，是「走进」他人土地的名词。

items.en: The verb vadere meant "to go" and appears in many motion words.
items.cn: 动词 vadere 意为「走」，出现在许多表示移动的词中。

items.en: in- added direction to it, giving invadere, "to go into".
items.cn: in- 给它加上方向，构成 invadere「走进去」。

items.en: The noun invasio named the act of entering, often hostilely.
items.cn: 名词 invasio 指进入的行为，常带敌意。

items.en: French reshaped the noun as invasion before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语先把该名词改写成 invasion，英语再借入。

items.en: English kept the military sense and added the privacy sense in legal use.
items.cn: 英语保留军事义，又在法律用法中添了隐私义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inva-/inve- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for hostile entry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 inva-/inve- 开头；近义组收表示敌意进入的词。

entries.definition: The act of avoiding something by trickery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「逃避」，靠花招躲开。

entries.definition: Something newly created or made up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发明；捏造」。

entries.definition: The act of turning something upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「倒置」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: A sudden violent attempt to hurt or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「攻击」，强调突然动手。

entries.definition: A short sudden attack into enemy ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「突袭」，短促而突然。

entries.definition: An unwanted arrival into a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「闯入」，强调不受欢迎。

normalIntro.en: These hooks attach the word to border crossings you can picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你想象得出的越界画面上。

normal.en: in- means into, and vad- means go.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vad- 是「走」。

normal.en: in + vad + ion: the going into a place.
normal.cn: in + vad + ion：走进一个地方这件事。

normal.en: An invasion force is the group that does the going in.
normal.cn: 入侵部队就是负责走进去的那批人。

normal.en: Invasion is invasion only when the door was not opened.
normal.cn: 门不是自己打开的，才叫入侵。

normal.en: Its verb is invade, which drops the -sion.
normal.cn: 它的动词是 invade，少了 -sion 那一截。

abstract.en: Invasion is a border crossed without permission.
abstract.cn: 入侵就是一条未经许可被越过的边界。

abstract.en: When a crowd becomes a tide, the word comes out.
abstract.cn: 当人群变成潮水，这个词就出场了。

abstract.en: Privacy has borders too, and letters are a wall.
abstract.cn: 隐私也有边界，信件就是一堵墙。

examples.en: The museum closed when news of the invasion reached the city.
examples.cn: 入侵的消息传到城里，博物馆就关门了。

examples.en: Critics called the camera in the changing room an invasion of privacy.
examples.cn: 批评者称更衣室里的摄像头侵犯了隐私。

examples.en: Every summer brings an invasion of insects to the lake.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，湖边都会被虫子大批占据。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vas（走）+ ion（名词）——踩进别人的地界

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vadere「走」→ invasio「进入」→ 法语 invasion → 英语 invasion。同族有 invade、invasive、invader。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: an army crossing in, taking over another land, breaking into privacy, and a flood of people or things.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：军队越境进入、侵占他国、侵犯隐私，以及人潮物潮的大量涌入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary being crossed from the outside by force.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界被外力从外面跨过。

branches.en: THE LANDING: troops stepping onto a foreign shore.
branches.cn: 登陆这条线：士兵踏上一片异国的海岸。

branches.en: THE FLOOD: numbers that pour in without welcome.
branches.cn: 潮水这条线：不受欢迎地涌来的人与物。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a private space entered without leave.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：未经允许进入的私人空间。

branches.en: THE LINE: both senses break a boundary they were not invited past.
branches.cn: 界线这条线：两个义项都越过了没被邀请越过的界。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: both senses take what belongs to someone else.
branches.cn: 占夺这条线：两个义项都拿走了属于别人的东西。

intro.en: Invasion is in- "into", the root vad- "go", and the noun ending -sion.
intro.cn: invasion 是 in-「进入」、词根 vad-「走」与名词词尾 -sion 的组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere and invasio are both recorded; the past participle invasus supplied the -s-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 与 invasio 均有记载，过去分词 invasus 提供了那个 -s-。

items.example: It points the motion inward.
The root survives in evade and pervade.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 evade 与 pervade。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor.
English kept the verb beside the noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把动词和名词并留着。

items.example: The ending -ive marks the tendency.
The ending -er names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 指做这事的人。

items.meaning: to go out of the way
items.example: The same root with e- for out gives the opposite motion.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根配 e-「向外」就成了反向动作。

definition_zh: 入侵性的；（物种）外来的、迅速扩散并造成损害的；侵入性的；（肿瘤）侵袭性的；侵犯的
definition_en: spreading into a place or body where it does not belong, especially of a species that spreads beyond its native range and causes harm
core_image: 一条堤岸被外来的藤蔓整片盖住，本地芦苇从下面透不出一片叶子，藤尖还在向水面探
scene: 外来的藤蔓沿着堤岸一路铺开，本地芦苇被压在下面几乎见不到光。Managers call the vine invasive because it smothers the native reeds.
sceneCN: 这里指外来物种迅速扩散并造成损害（第 1 个义项：侵入并扩散造成危害）；句意为管理者称这种藤为入侵性的，因为它把本地芦苇压死。

pos.zh: 入侵性的；外来的并造成损害的
侵入性的；侵袭性的（医学）

derivatives.zh: 该词的基座动词，由表示「进入」的前缀加表示「走」的词干构成，义为「侵入；侵袭」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「入侵；侵袭」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「入侵性；侵袭性」
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「非侵入性的」
由表示「最低限度」的副词与形容词构成，义为「微创的」

senses.title: Spreading beyond the native range and causing harm
senses.titleCN: 越出原生范围扩散并造成损害
senses.definition: of a species, spreading rapidly outside the range it evolved in and damaging the systems it enters
senses.definitionCN: 指物种在其演化范围之外迅速扩散，并损害它进入的系统
senses.example: The shrimp proved invasive in every estuary where it was released.
senses.exampleCN: 这种虾在每一个被放归的河口都表现出入侵性。
senses.why: The word pictures an entry by force, and ecology borrowed it for species that take ground rather than share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词画出「强行进入」的画面，生态学借它来形容那些夺取地面而非共享地面的物种。

senses.title: Not every introduced species is invasive
senses.titleCN: 并非所有引入物种都是入侵性的
senses.definition: describing harm and spread, not mere foreign origin, so a naturalised species that stays put is not called invasive
senses.definitionCN: 描述损害与扩散，而不是单纯的外来出身，因此安分定居的归化物种不被称为入侵性
senses.example: The poppy is introduced here but not invasive; it has stayed in the same fields for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这种罂粟在这里是引入种，却不是入侵性的；它在一个世纪里都待在同一片田里。
senses.why: Origin and behaviour are separate tests, and the word marks the second one.
senses.whyCN: 出身与行为是两套检验，这个词标记的是第二套。

senses.title: Entering the body in medical procedures
senses.definition: of a procedure or device, entering the body by puncture, incision or tube
senses.definitionCN: 指操作或器械以穿刺、切开或插管的方式进入体内
senses.example: The clinic replaced the open operation with a less invasive test.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把开刀手术换成了侵入性更小的检查。
senses.why: Medicine kept the physical sense of going in, and it measures how far the entry goes.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「进入」的字面意义，并衡量进入的程度。

senses.title: Spreading into surrounding tissue
senses.definition: of a tumour or infection, growing into nearby tissue rather than staying contained
senses.definitionCN: 指肿瘤或感染向邻近组织生长，而不是局限在原处
senses.example: The scan showed an invasive growth that had crossed the wall of the duct.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处已穿过管壁的侵袭性生长。
senses.why: Cancer that crosses a boundary is doing exactly what the Latin verb described: going in.
senses.whyCN: 越过边界的癌所做的正是那个拉丁动词所描述的：走进去。

senses.title: Intruding on privacy or rights
senses.definition: of a measure, technology or question, forcing its way into matters that should stay private
senses.definitionCN: 指措施、技术或提问强行进入本应私密的领域
senses.example: Staff called the new monitoring invasive and refused the ankle tags.
senses.exampleCN: 员工称新的监控侵犯个人，拒绝佩戴脚环。
senses.why: The metaphor needs no translation here: a boundary is crossed against the will of the person inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在这里无需翻译：边界是在里面那个人不情愿的情况下被越过的。

senses.title: Spreading vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: of a plant, growing and spreading so strongly that it displaces others
senses.definitionCN: 指植物生长扩散极强，以致挤走其他植物
senses.example: The reed is invasive in the marsh and has taken most of the open water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种芦苇在沼泽里扩散极强，已经占去了大部分明水。
senses.why: A plant that takes open water is behaving like an army taking ground, which is why the military word transferred.
senses.whyCN: 占据明水的植物，其行为像一支夺取地面的军队，这就是军事词会转过来的原因。

senses.title: Of military entry by force
senses.definition: of a force or operation, entering another territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 指力量或行动以武力进入他国领土
senses.example: The history course compared invasive campaigns across two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这门历史课比较了两个世纪里的入侵性军事行动。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal armed entry, and it remains available whenever a border is crossed by force.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是字面上的武装进入，只要边界被武力越过，这一义仍然可用。

senses.title: Of technologies that spread into new domains
senses.definition: of a tool or practice, spreading into areas where it was not expected and changing them
senses.definitionCN: 指工具或做法扩散到原本不被期待的领域并改变之
senses.example: Cheap sensors became invasive in daily life before any rule was written.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价传感器在任何人写规则之前就已经侵入日常生活。
senses.why: Tools spread the way organisms do, into spaces nobody assigned them, and the metaphor carries over.
senses.whyCN: 工具扩散的方式像生物一样，进入没人分给它们的空间，这个比喻因此顺手可用。

senses.title: A noun use for such organisms
senses.definition: in the plural, a shorthand for invasive plants or animals in management writing
senses.definitionCN: 在管理文本中以复数形式作为入侵植物或动物的简称
senses.example: The crew spent the summer pulling invasives from the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班组花了整个夏天从水道里拔除入侵物种。
senses.why: Field crews shorten long phrases, so the adjective became a plural noun meaning the plants and animals they pull.
senses.whyCN: 野外班组会缩短长短语，于是这个形容词成了复数名词，指他们拔除的动植物。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned adjective: a prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb to invade, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的形容词：表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成「侵入」，再加形容词词尾成为描述词。

items.en: Vadere meant to go or to proceed, and it supplied the movement at the heart of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为走、前行，提供了词的核心动作。

items.en: The compound meant to go into, enter or attack, and it was used of armies and of disease.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为走进、进入、攻击，用于军队，也用于疾病。

items.en: The adjective meant given to entering or attacking, and Late Latin used it in medical writing.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为好进入、好攻击的，晚期拉丁语在医学写作中使用它。

items.en: French carried the adjective onward, and English took it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词继续传下，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: Early English used it for armies and for arguments that encroached on another's ground.
items.cn: 早期英语用它指军队，也指侵占他人地盘的论点。

items.en: Ecologists applied it to organisms spreading beyond their native range with harmful effects; the usage settled in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 生态学家把它用于越出原生范围扩散并造成有害影响的生物；这一用法在二十世纪后期稳定下来。

note.en: The first group shares the going-in stem; the second group separates invasion from mere foreign origin.
note.cn: 第一组共用「走入」词干；第二组把入侵与单纯的外来出身区分开。

entries.definition: To enter by force, of armies, diseases or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指以强力进入，用于军队、疾病或生物。

entries.definition: The act of entering by force, and the event ecology counts.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入的行为，也是生态学所计的事件。

entries.definition: One that enters by force.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入者。

entries.definition: The quality of spreading and entering, measured in risk screening.
entries.definitionCN: 指扩散与进入的性质，在风险筛查中被度量。

entries.definition: Tending to avoid or escape; it shares the going verb but with a prefix for out.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向回避或逃开的；共用「走」动词，但前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: Present outside its native range, a statement about origin only.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于原生范围之外，只陈述出身。

entries.definition: Brought by people from elsewhere, without any claim about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指由人从别处带来，不含损害之意。

entries.definition: Advancing gradually into another's space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐侵占他人的空间或时间。

entries.definition: Pushing in where not wanted, common for privacy and devices.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入不受欢迎之处，常用于隐私与器械。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the going-in verb, the medical setting and the ecology test that separates origin from behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「走入」动词、医学场景，以及把出身与行为分开的生态学检验。

normal.en: Invade is go into, and invasive is the adjective of that going in.
normal.cn: 动词意为「走进去」，形容词就是这种进入的性质。

normal.en: Medicine asks how far the entry goes: open, minimally invasive, or no entry at all.
normal.cn: 医学问的是进入多深：开刀、微创，还是完全不进入。

normal.en: Alien and non-native state origin; invasive states behaviour and harm.
normal.cn: 「外来」陈述出身，「入侵性」陈述行为与损害。

normal.en: A naturalised poppy that stays in its field is not invasive, which is the commonest mistake.
normal.cn: 安分待在田里的归化罂粟不是入侵性的，这是最常见的错误。

normal.en: Minimally invasive is the fixed phrase that keeps the medical sense alive in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 「微创」是让医学义在日常语言里存活的固定说法。

abstract.en: Invasion is a claim about a boundary: the same movement is exploration in one frame and intrusion in another.
abstract.cn: 入侵是关于边界的判断：同样的移动，在一个框架里是探索，在另一个里是侵入。

abstract.en: Nature has no passports; the label is applied by the systems that receive the newcomer and pay for it.
abstract.cn: 自然界没有护照；这个标签由接收新来者并为之付出代价的那些系统贴上。

abstract.en: In medicine the word measures penetration of a body, in ecology penetration of a community: the geometry is the same.
abstract.cn: 医学上它度量对身体穿透，生态学上度量对群落的穿透：几何形状是一样的。

examples.en: The council removed the invasive shrub from the dune system.
examples.cn: 委员会清除了沙丘系统中的这种入侵灌木。

examples.en: Surgeons now prefer the less invasive route through the wrist.
examples.cn: 外科医生现在更青睐经手腕的侵入性较小的路径。

examples.en: Residents objected to the invasive questions at the checkpoint.
examples.cn: 居民反对检查站那些侵犯个人隐私的提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因维西夫」——因是进来，维西夫是走，走进别人的地盘还不走，就是入侵性的

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「走入、攻击」← in-「进入」→ 晚期拉丁语 invasivus「好进入的」→ 法语 invasif → 英语十七世纪借入。二十世纪后期生态学用它指越出原生范围扩散并造成损害的外来生物，此前主要指军事与医学上的侵入。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement of going in: the ecological spread, the origin test it is not, three kinds of physical entry, plants, armies, technology and a shorthand noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟随同一个「走入」的动作：生态扩散、它并不等同于的出身检验、三种实体进入、植物、军队、技术与名词简称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreign vine sheets the bank, cutting light from the reeds below while its tips reach the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条外来藤蔓铺满堤岸，把下面的芦苇遮死，藤尖还探向水面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL SPREAD: a species taking ground, and a plant growing strongly enough to displace others.
branches.cn: 生态扩散：物种夺取地面，以及植物长到足以挤走其他植物。

branches.en: THE TEST IT IS NOT: foreign origin alone, which introduced and naturalised species also have.
branches.cn: 它并不等同的检验：单纯的外来出身，引入与归化物种同样具备。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL ENTRY: a procedure entering the body, and a growth crossing into tissue.
branches.cn: 医学进入：操作进入体内，以及生长越入组织。

branches.en: THE OTHER INTRUSIONS: privacy, armed force, and tools spreading into unexpected domains.
branches.cn: 其他侵入：隐私、武力，以及扩散到意外领域的工具。

branches.en: THE SHORTHAND: invasives as the working noun of removal crews.
branches.cn: 简称：清除班组日常工作用语中的「入侵物种」。

intro.en: A prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成动词，形容词词尾构成描述词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vadere, invadere, invasio and invasivus; the recorded chain runs without gaps.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「走」「走入」「进入」与「好进入的」等形式，有记录的链条中间没有断口。

items.example: It marks movement across a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 它标记越过边界的移动。

items.example: It supplies the movement in the word.
It is the recorded source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是动词有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是形容词有记录的来源。

items.example: It turns the participle into a description.
It makes the noun for the entry.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示进入的名词。

items.example: It names the one entering.
It names the quality measured in screening.
items.exampleCN: 它命名筛查中所度量的性质。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from in- and vadere

derivatives.zh: 由该前缀加表示「走」的词干构成，义为「侵入」
由该动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「入侵」
由该动词加施动名词词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「非侵入性的」

definition_zh: 发明；发明物；编造；创造力
definition_en: the act of creating something new, the thing created, or something made up rather than true
core_image: 桌上散着齿轮、绳子和纸片，忽然拼成一个会转的小装置
scene: 车库里堆满拆开的零件，一个人把最后一根线接上，机器嗡嗡转了起来。The telephone was not one person's invention alone.
sceneCN: 这里 invention 是「发明」（第 1 个义项：创造新事物这件事），句意为电话并非某一个人的发明。画面里的物件：齿轮、线圈、工作台。

pos.zh: 名词：发明；发明物；编造；创造力

collocations.phrase: necessity is the mother of invention

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「发明；编造」
由 invent 加 -or 构成，义为「发明者」
由 invent 加 -ive 构成，义为「有创造力的」
形近同源词，义为「清单；存货」

senses.title: The act of creating
senses.titleCN: 把新东西造出来的那件事
senses.definition: the act of designing and making something that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 设计并制造出此前并不存在之物的行为
senses.example: The invention of the wheel changed travel for ever.
senses.exampleCN: 车轮的发明永远改变了出行。
senses.why: Latin invenire meant to come upon; an invention is something found by searching.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invenire 意为「碰上、发现」，invention 是找出来的东西。

senses.title: The thing created
senses.definition: a device, process, or idea that someone has created
senses.definitionCN: 由某人创造出来的器具、方法或想法
senses.example: Her latest invention folds into the size of a book.
senses.exampleCN: 她最新的发明能折成一本书那么大。
senses.why: The noun points at the object as easily as at the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指行为，也能直接指向那个物件。

senses.title: Something made up
senses.definition: a story or claim that is false and deliberately created
senses.definitionCN: 故意编造出来的虚假说法或故事
senses.example: The whole interview, he said, was an invention.
senses.exampleCN: 他说那篇采访整篇都是编造的。
senses.why: If inventing means making from nothing, a lie is an invention too.
senses.whyCN: 如果发明就是从无到有，那么谎言也是一种发明。

senses.title: Creative power
senses.definition: the ability to think of new things and make them
senses.definitionCN: 想出并做出新事物的能力
senses.example: The job calls for invention more than routine.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作靠的是创造力，而不是按部就班。
senses.why: The abstract sense names the faculty rather than any one product.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义指的是这种能力，而不是某件产品。

intro.en: Invention comes from Latin invenire, to come upon something by searching.
intro.cn: invention 来自拉丁语 invenire，意为通过寻找而碰上某物。

items.en: Venire meant to come; in- meant into or upon.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，in- 意为「进入、朝向」。

items.en: Invenire meant to find or to come across.
items.cn: invenire 意为找到或偶然碰上。

items.en: Inventio named the finding, later the making of something new.
items.cn: inventio 指「找到」，后来指造出新东西。

items.en: French invention kept both finding and devising.
items.cn: 法语 invention 兼有「发现」与「设计」。

items.en: English used invention for machines, stories, and talent.
items.cn: 英语用 invention 指机器、故事与才能。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vent- coming stem; the near-meaning group holds words for new creations.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vent-「来」词干；近义组收表示新造之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb of creating something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」。

entries.definition: The person who creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发明者」。

entries.definition: A coming between, from the same venire.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「干预」，同出 venire。

entries.definition: Finding something that already existed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发现」，对象本已存在。

entries.definition: Bringing something into being, often artistic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「创造」，偏艺术。

entries.definition: A machine made for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「装置」，是发明的实物形态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of parts coming together into something that works.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「零件拼成一件能转起来的东西」的画面。

normal.en: Invention is invent plus -ion, the act made into a thing.
normal.cn: invention 是 invent 加 -ion，动作变成了东西。

normal.en: The same venire is inside intervention and event.
normal.cn: 同一个 venire 也在 intervention 与 event 里。

normal.en: To invent can also mean to make up a story.
normal.cn: to invent 也可以指编故事。

normal.en: A patent protects an invention, not an idea in the air.
normal.cn: 专利保护的是发明，而不是空中的念头。

normal.en: The proverb says need is the mother of invention.
normal.cn: 谚语说，需要是发明之母。

abstract.en: An invention is an argument with the world that ends in a tool.
abstract.cn: 发明是一场与世界的争论，最后落成一件工具。

abstract.en: Finding and making share one Latin word for a reason.
abstract.cn: 发现与制造共用一个拉丁词，自有道理。

abstract.en: Every lie is a small invention with no patent.
abstract.cn: 每个谎言都是一项没申请专利的小发明。

examples.en: The invention of the printing press made books cheap.
examples.cn: 印刷机的发明让书变便宜了。

examples.en: The story about the ghost was pure invention.
examples.cn: 关于鬼的那个故事纯属编造。

examples.en: Her job rewards invention rather than obedience.
examples.cn: 她的工作看重创造力，而不是听话。

dict_mnemonic.text: invent（发明）+ ion（名词）——新造出来的东西

root: 拉丁语 venire「来」→ invenire「碰上、找到」→ inventio「发现、创制」→ 古法语 → 英语 invention。同族有 invent、inventor、inventory。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the act of creating, the thing created, a deliberate lie, and inventive power.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：创造这一行为、造出来的东西、故意编造，以及创造的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose parts on a bench suddenly moving together as a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：工作台上散着的零件忽然合成一台转动的机器。

branches.en: THE WORKBENCH: the act of designing something new.
branches.cn: 工作台这条线：设计新东西的过程。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: the object that resulted.
branches.cn: 装置这条线：最终得到的那件东西。

branches.en: THE TALE: a story invented out of nothing.
branches.cn: 故事这条线：从无中生出的说法。

branches.en: THE MIND: the talent for finding new ways.
branches.cn: 头脑这条线：找到新办法的才能。

branches.en: THE LINK: act and object wear the same name.
branches.cn: 连接线：行为与物件共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Invention is in- plus the root vent- "come" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: invention 由 in- 加词根 vent-「来」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin invenire and inventio are recorded forms of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invenire 与 inventio 是同一族的记载形式。

items.example: It turns coming into finding.
The root also appears in event and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 event 与 prevent。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The noun gives the abstract sense.
It builds the English noun.
It forms inventor.
It forms inventive.

items.meaning: a list of what is found
items.example: It keeps the older finding sense.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了更早的「找到」义。

definition_zh: 存货；库存；清单、目录；盘点；（把……）列入清单
definition_en: goods held in stock, or a full list of items recorded one by one
core_image: 仓库门被拉开，每一格里的东西都被记在同一张表上，表与实物一一对应
scene: 盘点员拿着表走过货架，把每一格的数量念出来，表上的数字与格子里的实物一一对上。The inventory showed far more unsold stock than the accounts suggested.
sceneCN: 盘点员沿货架逐格清点，把数量记在表上，纸面数字与实物一一对应；句中的 inventory 指「仓中现存的全部存货」（第 1 个义项：尚未售出、实际存放在库的商品与原料）。图中可辨识物件：盘点表、货架、纸箱、记号笔。

derivatives.zh: 已列入清单的
清点存货的过程
清单的；存货的

senses.title: Goods held in stock
senses.definition: the goods and materials a business keeps on hand for sale or production
senses.definitionCN: 企业为出售或生产而现存的货物与原料
senses.example: The inventory showed far more unsold stock than the accounts suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 盘点显示未售出的存货远多于账面上的数字。
senses.why: the word first meant a list of what was found, and the goods on the list took over the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「找到之物」的清单，清单上的货物后来接管了这个名字。

senses.title: A list of items
senses.titleCN: 逐项列出的清单或目录
senses.definition: a detailed list of goods, property or objects, item by item
senses.definitionCN: 逐项开列货物、财产或物品的详细清单
senses.example: The museum keeps an inventory of every coin in the vault.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆为库房里的每一枚硬币留有清单。
senses.why: this is the oldest sense: an inventory is literally that which has been come upon and written down.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：清单字面上就是「被发现并记下来」的东西。

senses.title: Stock as an asset
senses.titleCN: 会计上列为资产的存货
senses.definition: the value of unsold goods carried as a current asset on a balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 未售货物作为流动资产列在资产负债表上的价值
senses.example: Slow inventory tied up the company's cash for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 滞销库存把公司的现金占用了一整年。
senses.why: accounting turns the physical stock into a number, and keeps the same word for it.
senses.whyCN: 会计把实物存货变成一个数字，却仍用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: The act of counting stock
senses.definition: the process of counting and checking everything held in stock
senses.definitionCN: 逐件清点并核对库存的过程
senses.example: The shop closes early on the last day for inventory.
senses.exampleCN: 店铺在盘点那天提前关门。
senses.why: the noun of result became a noun of action, as happens with many words for lists and records.
senses.whyCN: 结果名词变成了动作名词，这在许多表示清单与记录的词中都会发生。

senses.title: To list and count
senses.titleCN: 编制清单、逐项清点（动词）
senses.definition: to make a complete list of something or to count stock item by item
senses.definitionCN: 为某物编制完整清单，或逐件清点存货
senses.example: Staff inventoried the shelves before the refit.
senses.exampleCN: 改装之前，员工清点了货架上的货。
senses.why: the verb simply applies the list-making act to the object being listed.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把「造清单」的动作施加到被列的对象上。

senses.title: Stock management as a function
senses.titleCN: 作为管理职能的库存控制
senses.definition: the function of deciding how much stock to hold and when to reorder
senses.definitionCN: 决定持有多少存货、何时补货的管理职能
senses.example: Inventory control cut the average holding time by half.
senses.exampleCN: 库存控制把平均持有时间缩短了一半。
senses.why: once stock is measured, it can be managed, and the word attaches to that managerial function.
senses.whyCN: 存货一旦可以计量，就可以被管理，这个词于是附在这一管理职能上。

senses.title: A scored questionnaire
senses.titleCN: 心理学中逐项评分的人格量表
senses.definition: a set of scored questions used to measure traits such as personality or depression
senses.definitionCN: 用逐项评分来测量人格或抑郁等特征的一套题目
senses.example: The personality inventory flagged high anxiety but normal mood.
senses.exampleCN: 这份人格量表显示焦虑偏高，情绪则属正常。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the list sense: a person is checked item by item, as goods are on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用了清单义：人被逐项核对，正如货架上的货被逐件清点。

senses.title: A full assessment of one's resources
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对自身资源与处境的全面清点
senses.definition: a careful review of what one has, whether skills, debts or memories
senses.definitionCN: 对自己拥有之物——技能、债务或记忆——的仔细梳理
senses.example: At fifty she took inventory of her life and changed course.
senses.exampleCN: 五十岁时她清点了自己的人生，随后改变了方向。
senses.why: the image of counting every item generalizes to counting everything one has, including what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 逐件清点的意象被一般化，用来数自己拥有的一切，包括看不见的东西。

intro.en: Inventory comes from Medieval Latin inventorium 'a list of things found', built on the Latin verb invenire 'to come upon, find'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inventory 来自中世纪拉丁语 inventorium「所列之物的清单」，其词根是拉丁语动词 invenire「遇到、发现」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Venire 'to come' is the base verb; the prefix in- adds the idea of coming upon something.
items.cn: venire「来」是基础动词，前缀 in- 增添「碰上、遇到」的意思。

items.en: Invenire meant 'to come upon, find, discover', and its participle inventum supplied the stem of the later noun.
items.cn: invenire 意为「遇到、找到、发现」，其分词 inventum 提供了后来名词的词干。

items.en: Medieval Latin inventorium named a written list of goods or property found on an estate, drawn up item by item.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 inventorium 指对某处产业中查得之物逐项开列的书面清单。

items.en: English adopted the word in the fifteenth century for such a list, and later for the goods themselves and the act of counting them.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪采用这个词指这类清单，后来又用它指货物本身以及清点的动作。

items.en: With industrial retailing, inventory became a managed asset, and the word moved into accounting, logistics and computing.
items.cn: 随着工业化零售，存货成为被管理的资产，这个词也进入会计、物流与计算机领域。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same 'find' root that are often confused; group two holds words for goods held or for lists.
note.cn: 第一组同出「发现」这一词根，常被混淆；第二组指持有之物或清单。

entries.definition: The same verb 'to come upon': to devise something that did not exist, originally to find it out.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「遇到」这一动词：创造出原先没有的东西，原义是把它找出来。

entries.definition: The act or product of devising something new, from the same stem as inventory.
entries.definitionCN: 设计出新事物的动作或产物，与 inventory 同出一个词干。

entries.definition: The one who devises something new; the ending marks a person, where inventory marks a list.
entries.definitionCN: 设计出新事物的人；词尾标记人，而 inventory 标记清单。

entries.definition: Able to devise new things, built on the same stem with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 能够设计出新事物的，由同一词干加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Goods kept for sale, the usual British term where American business says inventory.
entries.definitionCN: 为出售而持有的货物；英式常用这个词，美式商业则用 inventory。

entries.definition: A large store built up deliberately, often of essentials; it stresses accumulation over routine stock.
entries.definitionCN: 有意囤积的大量储备，常指必需品；强调积累而非日常库存。

entries.definition: A list of items arranged for reference or sale; an inventory is a list for checking and control.
entries.definitionCN: 为查阅或销售而编排的物品清单；inventory 是为核对与控制而作的清单。

entries.definition: The book of accounts; an inventory counts goods, a ledger records money.
entries.definitionCN: 账册；inventory 清点货物，ledger 记录钱款。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real 'find' root, the real business phrases and the real psychological use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「发现」词根、真实的商业搭配与真实的心理测量用法。

normal.en: The root means 'to come upon': an inventory is what you find when you go through every shelf.
normal.cn: 词根意为「遇到、发现」：清单就是你走遍每个货架后查到的东西。

normal.en: The family runs invent, invention, inventor and inventive, all from the same 'find' stem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括发明、发明物、发明家与有创造力的，都出同一「发现」词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: inventory control, inventory turnover, take inventory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这个词：库存控制、存货周转、盘点。

normal.en: British shops say stock where American accounts say inventory.
normal.cn: 英国店铺多说 stock，美国会计多说 inventory。

normal.en: A personality inventory checks a person item by item, like goods on a shelf.
normal.cn: 人格量表逐项检查一个人，正如逐件清点货架上的货。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard that turns a room full of objects into numbered lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写字板，把满屋的东西变成一行行编号。

abstract.en: Picture a life laid out on a table and counted like coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一段人生被摊在桌上，像硬币一样被清点。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse whose shelves are questions rather than boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，货架上放的不是箱子而是问题。

examples.en: The warehouse holds two months of inventory at all times.
examples.cn: 这座仓库始终保有两个月的存货。

examples.en: They took inventory and found a third of the stock missing.
examples.cn: 他们盘点后发现三分之一的存货不见了。

examples.en: Inventory turnover tells you how quickly goods are sold.
examples.cn: 存货周转率说明货物卖得有多快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（在内）+ vent（来）+ ory」——把里面查到的东西都记下来 → 清单、存货

root: 中世纪拉丁语 inventorium（查得之物的清单）来自拉丁语 invenire（遇到、找到）＝in-（向内、在上）＋venire（来）。同族词有 invent、invention、inventor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a list of things found and then follow the goods on that list into accounting, management, psychology and finally into a private accounting of one's own life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「查得之物的清单」开始，再让清单上的货物走进会计、管理、心理学，最后走进一个人对自己人生的私下清点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clipboard that turns a room of objects into numbered lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写字板，把满屋物品变成一行行编号。

branches.en: FOUND AND LISTED: the goods and the list are two sides of the same act of finding.
branches.cn: 查到并记下：货物与清单是同一个「查」的动作的两面。

branches.en: MEASURED AND MANAGED: once counted, stock becomes an asset and then a function.
branches.cn: 计量与管理：一旦被清点，存货就成为资产，随后成为一项职能。

branches.en: THE COUNT ITSELF: the noun of result turns into a noun and then a verb of counting.
branches.cn: 清点本身：结果名词转为动作名词，再转为动词。

branches.en: A PERSON SCORED: psychology counts a person as a shop counts goods.
branches.cn: 被评分的人：心理学数人，正如店铺数货。

branches.en: ONE'S OWN LEDGER: the last count is of resources that never sat on a shelf.
branches.cn: 自己的账：最后一次清点的是从未上过货架的资源。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb and a medieval noun ending, and the family is shared with invention.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词与一个中世纪名词词尾构成，与「发明」一族共享词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire gives invent, invention and inventory; the prefix marks finding, and the ending marks a place or collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire 衍生出「发明」「发明物」与「清单」；前缀标记「找到」，词尾标记处所或集合。

items.example: The prefix turns coming into coming upon something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「来」变成「碰上某物」。

items.structure: venire, veni, ventum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)
items.example: The root is the plain verb of motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是表示移动的普通动词。

items.example: Invenire is the act behind both invention and inventory.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既是「发明」也是「清单」背后的动作。

items.example: The participle supplies the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了名词词干。

items.example: The medieval list named every item on the estate.
items.exampleCN: 这份中世纪清单列出了产业上的每一项。

items.example: The inventory filled three pages.
She invented a quieter pump.
items.exampleCN: 她发明了一种更安静的泵。

items.meaning: the act or product of devising
items.example: The invention changed the trade.
items.exampleCN: 这项发明改变了这个行业。

items.example: Every crate was inventoried.
items.exampleCN: 每一只箱子都被登记在册。

latinEntries.structure: inventorium, inventori (n., second declension, Medieval Latin)
