definition_zh: 无脊椎动物；无脊椎的
definition_en: an animal without a backbone, or lacking a backbone
core_image: 退潮的水洼里，一团没有骨架的软体摊在石上，靠水支撑着形状
scene: 退潮后的水洼里，一只没有骨架的软体动物摊在石头上，靠残留的水维持形状。 Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on the water to hold its shape.
sceneCN: 这里 invertebrate 指「无脊椎动物」（第 1 个义项：没有脊柱的动物）；句意为由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物只能靠水来维持体形。

derivatives.zh: 无脊椎动物（复数）
无脊椎动物学
无脊椎动物类群（旧分类名）
脊椎动物；有脊椎的

senses.title: An animal without a backbone
senses.definition: any animal that lacks a vertebral column, including insects, worms, mollusks and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 任何没有脊柱的动物，包括昆虫、蠕虫、软体动物与甲壳动物
senses.example: Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on water to hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物靠水维持体形。
senses.why: The word is literally 'without vertebrae': in- 'not' plus vertebra, the bones of the spine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「没有脊椎」：in-「不」加 vertebra（脊柱的骨节）。

senses.title: The adjective: lacking a backbone
senses.definition: describing an animal or body plan that has no spinal column
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有脊柱的动物或身体结构
senses.example: The invertebrate body plan allows bending in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎的身体结构允许向各个方向弯曲。
senses.why: English uses the same form for noun and adjective, so the ending -ate does double duty.
senses.whyCN: 英语中名词与形容词同形，因此 -ate 词尾同时承担两种功能。

senses.title: The field of invertebrate zoology
senses.titleCN: 无脊椎动物学这一学科
senses.definition: the branch of zoology that studies animals without backbones
senses.definitionCN: 研究无脊柱动物的动物学分支
senses.example: Invertebrate zoology covers far more species than vertebrate zoology.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎动物学涵盖的物种远多于脊椎动物学。
senses.why: Because most animal species lack a backbone, the adjective became a discipline label.
senses.whyCN: 由于大多数动物物种没有脊柱，这个形容词成了一个学科标签。

senses.title: A fossil invertebrate
senses.definition: ancient remains of an animal without a backbone, often shells or exoskeletons
senses.definitionCN: 无脊柱动物的古代遗骸，常为贝壳或外骨骼
senses.example: The oldest invertebrate fossils are more than half a billion years old.
senses.exampleCN: 最古老的无脊椎动物化石已有五亿多年历史。
senses.why: Hard shells and exoskeletons preserve far better than soft vertebrate tissue, so the fossil record is dominated by invertebrates.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳与外骨骼比脊椎动物的软组织更易保存，因此化石记录以无脊椎动物为主。

senses.title: A marine invertebrate
senses.definition: an invertebrate living in the sea, such as a coral, crab or sea worm
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的无脊椎动物，如珊瑚、蟹或海虫
senses.example: Marine invertebrates build most of the reef structure.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋无脊椎动物建造了大部分礁体结构。
senses.why: Ecology uses the category because reef builders and sea-floor communities cross many phyla.
senses.whyCN: 生态学使用这一范畴，因为造礁者与海底群落跨越许多门。

senses.title: A source of food and stock
senses.definition: an invertebrate harvested or farmed for food, such as shrimp, squid or oysters
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞或养殖的无脊椎动物，如虾、鱿鱼或牡蛎
senses.example: Most aquaculture production is invertebrate.
senses.exampleCN: 水产养殖的大部分产量来自无脊椎动物。
senses.why: The category groups together very different edible animals that share only the absence of a spine.
senses.whyCN: 这一范畴把差异极大、只共享「没有脊柱」这一点的可食动物归在一起。

senses.title: Figurative: lacking firmness or courage
senses.definition: describing a person or organization seen as weak-willed or lacking firm principles
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人或组织意志软弱、缺乏坚定原则
senses.example: Critics called the committee invertebrate for postponing the decision again.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说委员会又一次推迟决定，毫无骨气。
senses.why: The metaphor takes 'no backbone' from anatomy and applies it to character: no spine, no resolve.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把解剖上的「没有脊柱」用到性格上：没有脊梁，就没有决断。

senses.title: A bioindicator community
senses.definition: invertebrates used to assess water or soil quality because they respond quickly to pollution
senses.definitionCN: 因对污染反应迅速而被用来评估水或土壤质量的无脊椎动物
senses.example: Stream invertebrates are sampled to grade water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 通过采样溪流无脊椎动物来评定水质。
senses.why: Monitoring programs use the category because mayflies, snails and worms together signal different pollution levels.
senses.whyCN: 监测项目使用这一范畴，因为蜉蝣、螺与蠕虫共同指示不同的污染水平。

intro.en: Invertebrate is Latin in- 'not' plus vertebra 'joint of the spine', with the adjective ending -ate; the word is a modern scientific formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: invertebrate 由拉丁 in-「不」加 vertebra「脊柱的骨节」，再加形容词词尾 -ate 构成；它是近代科学造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertebra meant a joint, especially a joint of the spine, from vertere 'to turn'. The link to 'turn' is generally accepted; the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: vertebra 意为「关节」，尤指脊柱的关节，来自 vertere「转动」。与「转动」的联系一般被接受；更深的词根属重构。

items.en: The prefix in- 'not' negates the noun, so an invertebrate is literally 'one without vertebrae'.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「不」否定该名词，因此 invertebrate 字面就是「没有脊椎的东西」。

items.en: Lamarck's early nineteenth-century classification used invertébrés for animals without a spinal column, and English borrowed the term.
items.cn: 拉马克在 19 世纪初的分类中使用 invertébrés 指没有脊柱的动物，英语借入了这个词。

items.en: English invertebrate appears in the nineteenth century as both noun and adjective, in zoology and in general prose.
items.cn: 英语 invertebrate 在 19 世纪出现，既作名词也作形容词，见于动物学与一般散文。

items.en: By the later nineteenth century 'no backbone' was applied to people and institutions lacking firmness, and the figurative sense entered dictionaries.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪后期，「没有脊梁」被用于形容缺乏坚定性的人与机构，比喻义进入词典。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin root of vertere is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 vertere 的拉丁语之前词根属重构，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same vertebra stock that are easily confused; group two holds animal-category words that overlap with invertebrate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vertebra 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是与无脊椎动物重叠的动物范畴词。

entries.definition: An animal with a backbone; it differs from invertebrate by the single negative prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 有脊柱的动物；与 invertebrate 只差一个否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: A single bone of the spine; several are vertebrae. The animal word is built on this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 脊柱的一块骨；多块为 vertebrae。动物词正是在这个名词上构成的。

entries.definition: Relating to a vertebra or the spine, as in vertebral column; it is not the animal category word.
entries.definitionCN: 与椎骨或脊柱有关，如 vertebral column；它不是动物类别词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to turn upside down, from in- + vertere 'turn'; it shares the root but is not related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为翻转，由 in- + vertere「转」构成；同词根，但意义无关。

entries.definition: A jointed-legged invertebrate; arthropods are the largest subgroup of invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；节肢动物是最大的无脊椎动物亚群。

entries.definition: A soft-bodied invertebrate, usually with a shell; another subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物；另一个亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A segmented worm such as an earthworm; it is one kind of invertebrate among very many.
entries.definitionCN: 分节的蠕虫，如蚯蚓；它是众多无脊椎动物中的一类。

entries.definition: Small drifting animals in water, many of them invertebrates; the term names a lifestyle, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 水中漂浮的小型动物，许多是无脊椎动物；这个词命名生活方式，而不是类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'not' + vertebrate 'backboned': the animal with no spine.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ vertebrate「有脊椎的」：没有脊柱的动物。

normal.en: Vertebra is one spinal bone; vertebrae are several; invertebrate means none at all.
normal.cn: vertebra 是一块椎骨，vertebrae 是多块，invertebrate 则一块也没有。

normal.en: Most animal species are invertebrates: insects alone outnumber all vertebrates.
normal.cn: 大多数动物物种是无脊椎动物：仅昆虫就超过所有脊椎动物。

normal.en: The figurative use is 'no backbone' in character, not in anatomy.
normal.cn: 比喻义指性格上「没有脊梁」，而非解剖结构。

normal.en: Invertebrate zoology is a field name, because the category covers dozens of phyla.
normal.cn: invertebrate zoology 是学科名，因为这一范畴涵盖数十个门。

abstract.en: Picture a body that holds itself up with water instead of bone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用水的力量而不是骨头来支撑的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a committee with no spine, bending whichever way the wind blows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有脊梁的委员会，风往哪吹就往哪倒。

abstract.en: Picture a mayfly in a stream acting as a tiny water-quality meter.
abstract.cn: 想象溪流里一只蜉蝣，充当一枚微小的水质计。

examples.en: Invertebrates make up roughly ninety-five per cent of animal species.
examples.cn: 无脊椎动物约占动物物种的百分之九十五。

examples.en: The survey recorded invertebrates but no vertebrates in the polluted stream.
examples.cn: 调查在被污染的溪流中记录到无脊椎动物，却没有脊椎动物。

examples.en: The minister was called invertebrate for refusing to defend the policy.
examples.cn: 这位部长因拒绝为该政策辩护而被称为没有骨气。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vertebrate（有脊椎的）——没有脊椎的动物；记「软体、虫、虾蟹都不靠脊梁」

root: 拉丁 in-「不」+ vertebra「脊椎骨节」（源自 vertere「转动」）+ -ate；vertebra 的更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one negative fact, the absence of a spine, through zoology, palaeontology, ecology, fisheries, metaphor and pollution monitoring.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕一个否定事实——没有脊柱，穿过动物学、古生物学、生态学、渔业、比喻与污染监测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft body in a tide pool, held up by water rather than bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里一具柔软的身体，靠水而非骨骼支撑。

branches.en: ABSENCE: noun and adjective both say the same thing, that there is no vertebral column.
branches.cn: 缺失：名词与形容词说的是同一件事——没有脊柱。

branches.en: A FIELD: because the category is so wide, it becomes a branch of zoology.
branches.cn: 一个学科：范畴太宽，于是成了一门动物学分支。

branches.en: HARD PARTS IN SOFT ANIMALS: shells and exoskeletons dominate the fossil and reef records.
branches.cn: 软体中的硬部件：贝壳与外骨骼主导了化石与礁体记录。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND INSTRUMENT: food from the sea, and a meter for its health.
branches.cn: 资源与仪器：既是海中食物，也是衡量其健康的仪表。

branches.en: METAPHOR: no spine becomes no courage.
branches.cn: 比喻：没有脊柱变成了没有骨气。

intro.en: Invertebrate is a prefixed derivative of vertebra, so its parts are a negative prefix, a noun and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: invertebrate 是 vertebra 的加缀派生词，其成分是否定前缀、名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertebra comes from vertere 'to turn'; in- negates it, and -atus supplies the adjective shape that English reduced to -ate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertebra 来自 vertere「转动」；in- 加以否定，-atus 提供形容词形态，英语简化为 -ate。

items.example: The prefix denies the spine.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定了脊柱的存在。

items.example: Each vertebra turns slightly on the next.
items.exampleCN: 每块椎骨都能相对下一块略微转动。

items.example: The ending makes the word an adjective as well as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使该词兼作形容词与名词。

items.example: The invertebrate has no spinal column.
items.exampleCN: 这只无脊椎动物没有脊柱。

items.example: Invertebrates fill the stream bed.
Vertebrates are the minority of animal species.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物只占动物物种的少数。

items.example: The vertebral column protects the nerve cord.
Invert shares the turning root but not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: invert 同出「转」词根，但意义不同。

definition_zh: 投资；投入（时间精力）；授予（权力）
definition_en: to put money, time, or effort into something hoping for a return, or to formally give someone power or a right
core_image: 一笔钱被装进土里，等着日后长出更多
scene: 父亲把存折推到女儿面前，让她自己决定怎么用这笔学费之外的钱。She decided to invest half of it in a small bakery.
sceneCN: 这里 invest 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：把钱投出去以求回报），句意为她决定把其中一半投进一家小面包店。画面里的物件：存折、桌面、台灯。

pos.zh: 动词：投资；投入；授予权力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「投资；投资额」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
加前缀 di- 构成的反向词，义为「撤资；剥夺」
去掉 in- 的同源词，义为「背心；授予」

senses.title: Putting money to work
senses.definition: to put money into a business or asset in order to make a profit later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进企业或资产，指望日后获利
senses.example: They invested their savings in solar panels for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把积蓄投在了屋顶的太阳能板上。
senses.why: Latin investire meant "to clothe", and money clothed in a venture was said to be invested.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给穿衣」，钱被「穿」进一桩事业，就叫投了出去。

senses.title: Spending effort
senses.definition: to give time, energy, or attention to something because it matters
senses.definitionCN: 因为某事重要而付出时间、精力或注意力
senses.example: She invested three years in learning the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了三年时间学小提琴。
senses.why: If money can be dressed in a project, so can effort: both are resources you part with.
senses.whyCN: 钱能披挂在一个项目上，力气也行：两者都是你交出去的资源。

senses.title: Giving formal power
senses.definition: to give someone the official right or power to act in a role
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人在某职位上行动的权力
senses.example: The new mayor was invested with the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长被授予聘用员工的权力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is ceremonial: a robe was put on someone to show the office was now theirs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是仪式性的：给别人穿上礼服，表示职位从此归他。

intro.en: Invest began as a word about clothes and ceremony long before it meant money.
intro.cn: invest 在表示钱之前，长期是个关于衣服与仪式的词。

items.en: The noun vestis meant "garment".
items.cn: 名词 vestis 意为「衣服」。

items.en: investire meant "to put a garment on someone".
items.cn: investire 意为「给人穿上衣服」。

items.en: The Church used it for dressing a person in the robes of an office.
items.cn: 教会用它表示给人穿上某职位的礼服。

items.en: Trade turned the idea of clothing into placing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业把「穿衣」的想法转成了把钱放进一桩事业。

items.en: Banks and markets fixed the financial sense in everyday speech.
items.cn: 银行与市场把这一金融义固定进了日常语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vest- stem; the near-meaning group holds words about putting resources in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vest- 词干；近义组收表示投入资源的词。

entries.definition: A sleeveless garment worn under a jacket.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「背心」，同词根。

entries.definition: To sell off holdings or strip someone of power.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「撤资；剥夺」，反向词。

entries.definition: To create something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To provide money for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「资助」，提供资金。

entries.definition: To give time or attention completely to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「奉献」，强调全心全意。

entries.definition: To set money or resources aside for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「拨出」，指分配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move the word from a robe to a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词从礼服挪到钱包。

normal.en: in- means in, and vest- means clothes.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vest- 是「衣服」。

normal.en: Money is dressed in a project, so it is invested.
normal.cn: 钱被「穿」在项目上，所以叫投进去。

normal.en: What you put in is an investment.
normal.cn: 你放进去的那笔就叫 investment。

normal.en: The person who puts it in is an investor.
normal.cn: 放进去的人叫 investor。

normal.en: Dress effort in a cause and you invest in it too.
normal.cn: 把力气披挂在一件事上，也是 invest。

abstract.en: Investment is trust wearing a price tag.
abstract.cn: 投资是贴上价签的信任。

abstract.en: To invest is to plant and then leave the field alone.
abstract.cn: 投资是种下去，然后先别去动那块地。

abstract.en: Power, like money, is handed over by an act of dressing.
abstract.cn: 权力和钱一样，都靠一个「加衣」的动作交出去。

examples.en: The fund invests mainly in small farms.
examples.cn: 这只基金主要投资小型农场。

examples.en: He invested every spare hour in the repair of the boat.
examples.cn: 他把每一个空闲小时都投在了修船上。

examples.en: The board invested the director with full control of the budget.
examples.cn: 董事会授予这位主管完全的预算控制权。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vest（衣服）——把钱裹进项目里

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestis「衣服」→ investire「给穿衣」→ 中世纪拉丁语指授职 → 英语 invest 引申为「投资」。同族有 investment、investor、divest、vest。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting in money, putting in effort, and formally granting power.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：投入金钱、投入精力，以及正式授予权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something valuable is handed over and dressed in a new role.
core.cn: 核心意象：有价值的东西被交出去，并披上一个新的身份。

branches.en: THE PURSE: money placed where it can grow.
branches.cn: 钱包这条线：放在能生长之处的钱。

branches.en: THE HOURS: time given to a craft or cause.
branches.cn: 时间这条线：给一门手艺或一件事的时间。

branches.en: THE ROBE: official authority put on a person.
branches.cn: 礼服这条线：披在某人身上的官方权力。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: both senses part with something now for later.
branches.cn: 资源这条线：两个义项都是现在付出、以后收获。

branches.en: THE GRANT: both senses make a formal transfer of value.
branches.cn: 授予这条线：两个义项都完成一次正式的价值转移。

intro.en: Invest is in- "into" plus vestis "garment"; the robe may be worn by a man or by money.
intro.cn: invest 是 in-「进入」加 vestis「衣服」，穿上礼服的可能是人，也可能是钱。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis, vestire and investire are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis、vestire 与 investire 均有记载。

items.example: It puts the garment on.
The root names what is put on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被穿上的东西。

items.example: It forms investment.
It forms investor.
The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The bare stem still names a piece of clothing.
items.exampleCN: 光词干至今仍指一件衣服。

items.example: It builds divest, to strip away.
The prefix reverses the direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把方向反了过来。

definition_zh: 调查；研究；侦察
definition_en: to examine a situation, event, or person carefully in order to find out the truth
core_image: 一只手举着灯，在地上一点点照着找脚印
scene: 雨后的院子里，两个人蹲下来，用手电照着泥地，看脚印往哪个方向走。Police are investigating the cause of the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 investigate 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为查明真相而仔细查），句意为警方正在调查火灾的起因。画面里的物件：手电、泥地脚印、警戒线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「调查」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」
同源词，义为「痕迹」

senses.title: Look into a case
senses.definition: to try to find out the facts about a crime, accident, or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 设法查清犯罪、事故或投诉的事实
senses.example: Officers are investigating the break-in at the school.
senses.exampleCN: 警员正在调查学校那次闯入事件。
senses.why: Latin vestigium means a footprint, and the verb meant to follow footprints.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为「脚印」，那个动词意为「循脚印追查」。

senses.title: Study to understand
senses.definition: to examine something systematically in order to understand how it works
senses.definitionCN: 为理解其运作方式而系统地检视某事物
senses.example: Scientists are investigating why the lake is warming.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家正在研究这座湖为何变暖。
senses.why: The same footprint-following works for nature as for crime.
senses.whyCN: 循脚印追查既用于案件，也用于自然现象。

senses.title: Examine a person
senses.definition: to question or examine a person officially to judge their part in something
senses.definitionCN: 为判断某人在事件中的角色而正式讯问或审查
senses.example: Two managers were investigated over the payments.
senses.exampleCN: 两名经理因这些款项受到调查。
senses.why: People also leave tracks, so the verb turns from things to persons.
senses.whyCN: 人也会留下痕迹，于是这个动词从物转向人。

senses.title: Explore a possibility
senses.definition: to look into whether something is possible or true before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定之前先弄清某事是否可能或属实
senses.example: We should investigate whether the hall can hold two hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 我们该查一查礼堂能不能容纳两百人。
senses.why: The cautious sense checks facts before a decision is made.
senses.whyCN: 这种谨慎用法是在决定之前先核实。

intro.en: Investigate comes from Latin investigare, to follow footprints, from vestigium, a footprint.
intro.cn: investigate 来自拉丁语 investigare「循脚印追查」，源出 vestigium「脚印」。

items.en: Vestigium meant a footprint or a trace left behind.
items.cn: vestigium 意为脚印或留下的痕迹。

items.en: Investigare meant to track something by its traces.
items.cn: investigare 意为顺着痕迹追踪。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the tracing itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这番追踪。

items.en: English used investigate for legal and scholarly inquiry.
items.cn: 英语用 investigate 指法律与学术的查究。

items.en: Police work made it a familiar verb of daily news.
items.cn: 警务让它成为新闻里的常用动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for inquiry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 开头；近义组收表示查究的词。

entries.definition: The inquiry itself as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「调查」。

entries.definition: To put money into something for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，拼写近似。

entries.definition: A small remaining trace of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「残留的痕迹」，同出 vestigium。

entries.definition: To look at something closely and carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「检查」，偏细看。

entries.definition: To search into something awkward or hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「探究」，语气更锐利。

entries.definition: To try to find out about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「查一查」，偏口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the footprint at the heart of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用这个词心里的那只脚印。

normal.en: Vestigium means footprint; to investigate is to follow the prints.
normal.cn: vestigium 意为脚印；investigate 就是顺着脚印走。

normal.en: The same trace survives in vestige, a leftover mark.
normal.cn: 同样的痕迹留在 vestige 里，那是残余的印记。

normal.en: Police investigate crimes; scientists investigate causes.
normal.cn: 警察调查案件，科学家研究成因。

normal.en: Under investigation means the prints are still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是脚印还没凉。

normal.en: Do not mix it with invest, which is about money.
normal.cn: 别和 invest 混：那个词讲的是钱。

abstract.en: Investigation is patience with a lamp.
abstract.cn: 调查是举着灯的一点耐心。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a print somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都会在某处留下印子。

abstract.en: To investigate is to admit you do not yet know.
abstract.cn: 调查等于承认自己还不知道。

examples.en: The committee will investigate how the money was spent.
examples.cn: 委员会将调查这笔钱是如何花掉的。

examples.en: She investigated the strange noise in the attic.
examples.cn: 她去查了阁楼里那奇怪的声音。

examples.en: He was investigated twice and cleared both times.
examples.cn: 他两次受到调查，两次都洗清了。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestige（痕迹）+ ate——顺着痕迹查进去

root: 拉丁语 vestigium「脚印」→ investigare「循迹追查」→ 英语 investigate。同族有 investigation、investigator、vestige。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: look into a case, study how something works, examine a person, and test a possibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：查案、研究运作原理、审查某人，以及核实某种可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp on the ground, following prints through mud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏照在地上的灯，顺着泥里的脚印走。

branches.en: THE CASE: officers tracing what happened.
branches.cn: 案件这条线：警员追查发生了什么。

branches.en: THE LAKE: researchers tracing why it warms.
branches.cn: 湖这条线：研究者追查变暖的原因。

branches.en: THE MANAGER: a person questioned about payments.
branches.cn: 经理这条线：就款项受到询问的人。

branches.en: THE HALL: checking a fact before deciding.
branches.cn: 礼堂这条线：决定之前先核实。

branches.en: THE LINK: both follow traces towards a hidden cause.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都顺着痕迹追向隐藏的原因。

intro.en: Investigate is in- "in" plus the Latin stem vestig- "trace" and a verb ending.
intro.cn: investigate 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词干 vestig-「痕迹」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium, investigare and investigatio are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium、investigare 与 investigatio 均有记载。

definition_zh: 调查；侦查；研究
definition_en: a careful, formal attempt to find out the facts about an event, problem, or claim
core_image: 手电照着地面，一步步顺着脚印往里查
scene: 办公室里文件摊满桌面，两个人对着账本逐页核对日期。The investigation found that two payments had been recorded twice.
sceneCN: 这里 investigation 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为弄清事实而做的正式查证），句意为调查发现有两笔付款被记了两次。画面里的物件：账本、桌面、荧光笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 换 -ate，义为「调查；侦查」
由 investigate 加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由 investigate 词干加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」

senses.title: Official fact-finding
senses.definition: a formal process in which an authority examines evidence to establish the truth
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构审查证据、确定真相的正式过程
senses.example: A government investigation cleared the factory of any fault.
senses.exampleCN: 政府调查澄清这家工厂没有过错。
senses.why: Latin investigare meant "to follow the footprints", from in- plus vestigium, "track".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investigare 意为「跟着脚印走」，由 in- 加 vestigium「足迹」构成。

senses.title: Police or detective work
senses.definition: the work of police or detectives gathering facts about a suspected crime
senses.definitionCN: 警方或侦探就疑似犯罪收集事实的工作
senses.example: The investigation into the missing paintings lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失踪画作的侦查持续了四年。
senses.why: The footprint image fits best here: a detective literally follows a trail.
senses.whyCN: 「脚印」这个意象在这里最贴切：侦探就是顺着痕迹走的人。

senses.title: Careful study of a problem
senses.definition: a thorough academic or scientific study of a question
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题所作的详尽学术或科学研究
senses.example: Her investigation of soil bacteria changed the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她对土壤细菌的研究改变了这个领域。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word because a good study also follows traces until a pattern shows.
senses.whyCN: 科学借用了这个词，因为好的研究同样顺着痕迹走到规律显现。

intro.en: Investigation carries a picture of footprints: Latin vestigium means "track".
intro.cn: investigation 带着脚印的画面：拉丁语 vestigium 意为「足迹」。

items.en: vestigium meant "footprint, trace".
items.cn: vestigium 意为「脚印、痕迹」。

items.en: investigare meant "to follow a track".
items.cn: investigare 意为「跟着足迹走」。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the search itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这场追寻。

items.en: English took the noun for legal and official enquiries.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词用于法律与官方查问。

items.en: Science adopted it for systematic study as well.
items.cn: 科学界也采用它表示系统性研究。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vestigi- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for searching out facts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vestigi- 词干；近义组收表示查明事实的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to look into a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，同词干。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: A request to come somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请」，尾音相近。

entries.definition: A question or a formal look into facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「询问；查问」。

entries.definition: A close and often official examination.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「探查」，常指官方深入检查。

entries.definition: Systematic study to discover new facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究」，偏学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all walk along a set of footprints.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都沿着同一串脚印走。

normal.en: in- means into, and vestigium means footprint.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vestigium 是「脚印」。

normal.en: To investigate is to follow the prints in.
normal.cn: investigate 就是顺着脚印往里查。

normal.en: The noun investigation is the whole walk.
normal.cn: 名词 investigation 指这整段路。

normal.en: An investigator is the one holding the torch.
normal.cn: investigator 是那个举着手电的人。

normal.en: Under investigation means the trail is still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是痕迹还热着。

abstract.en: Investigation is doubt that refuses to stay lazy.
abstract.cn: 调查是不肯偷懒的怀疑。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a footprint; the word is the act of bending down.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都留下脚印；这个词就是弯腰去看。

abstract.en: A careful inquiry turns noise into a line.
abstract.cn: 仔细的查证把杂音拉成一条线。

examples.en: The investigation into the fire took almost a year.
examples.cn: 对那场火灾的调查花了将近一年。

examples.en: Two officers were suspended while under investigation.
examples.cn: 两名警员在接受调查期间被停职。

examples.en: Her investigation of the lake water found traces of lead.
examples.cn: 她对湖水的调查发现了微量的铅。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestig（脚印）+ ation（名词）——顺着脚印查到底

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestigium「足迹」→ investigare「跟踪追查」→ investigatio → 英语 investigation。同族有 investigate、investigator、investigative。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an official inquiry, police detective work, and a thorough study of a question.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方查证、警方侦查，以及对某个问题的深入研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: following a trail of footprints until the truth shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：顺着脚印走，直到真相显现。

branches.en: THE FILE: officials checking records against facts.
branches.cn: 档案这条线：官员把记录与事实对照。

branches.en: THE TRAIL: detectives walking a case to its end.
branches.cn: 痕迹这条线：侦探把一个案子走到底。

branches.en: THE LAB: researchers chasing a pattern through data.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：研究者在数据里追一个规律。

branches.en: THE PROOF: both senses need evidence that holds up.
branches.cn: 证据这条线：两个义项都要站得住的证据。

branches.en: THE METHOD: both senses proceed step by step.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：两个义项都一步一步推进。

intro.en: Investigation is in- "into", vestigium "track", -ate the verb ending, and -ion for the act.
intro.cn: investigation 由 in-「进入」、vestigium「足迹」、动词尾 -ate 与名词尾 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium and investigare are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 与 investigare 均有记载。

definition_zh: 投资；投资额；投入；投资物
definition_en: money put into something in order to gain a profit or benefit, or the act of putting it there
core_image: 一叠钱被放进一个还在长的树坑里，等着以后长出来
scene: 老人把攒下的钱投进一家小工厂，又花两年时间教工人手艺。The new road was a huge public investment.
sceneCN: 这里 investment 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：为获利而投入的钱或投入行为），句意为新道路是一项巨大的公共投资。画面里的物件：存折、树坑、工厂图纸。

pos.zh: 名词：投资；投资额；投入；投资物

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「投资」
由 invest 加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
由 invest 加 -ing 构成，义为「投资行为」
同源词，义为「授职仪式」

senses.title: Money put in for gain
senses.definition: money placed in a business, property, or scheme in the hope of earning more
senses.definitionCN: 为求得更多回报而投入企业、房产或项目的钱
senses.example: She made a small investment in a friend's bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家朋友的烘焙店做了小额投资。
senses.why: Latin investire meant to clothe; the money is dressed in a new form, hoping to grow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给……穿衣」，钱换了件衣裳，指望长大。

senses.title: The act of putting in
senses.definition: the act or process of putting money or effort into something
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或精力投入某事的行为或过程
senses.example: Investment in new machines rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年对新机器的投资大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun can name the deed rather than the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指动作，而不指金额。

senses.title: Time or effort given
senses.definition: time, energy, or care given to something in the belief that it will pay off
senses.definitionCN: 相信会有回报而在某事上给出的时间、精力或关心
senses.example: Learning the language was an investment of three years.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是三年的投入。
senses.why: Despite the money picture, the word readily counts hours as well as cash.
senses.whyCN: 尽管有金钱的画面，这个词同样能算小时，不限于现金。

senses.title: A thing invested in
senses.definition: a business, property, or asset in which money has been placed
senses.definitionCN: 已经投入资金的生意、房产或资产
senses.example: Their investments are mostly in land near the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的投资大多在城市近郊的土地上。
senses.why: By transfer the noun moves from the act to the holdings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 经转喻，名词从行为转到所持有的资产上。

intro.en: Investment comes from Latin investire, to clothe, through the idea of money put into a new dress.
intro.cn: investment 来自拉丁语 investire「给……穿衣」，经由「把钱换上新衣」的想法而来。

items.en: Vestire meant to clothe; in- meant into.
items.cn: vestire 意为穿衣，in- 意为进入。

items.en: Investire meant to dress someone in a robe of office.
items.cn: investire 意为给某人穿上就职礼袍。

items.en: English used invest for giving power or a rank.
items.cn: 英语用 invest 指授予权力或职位。

items.en: Commerce added the sense of dressing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业又添上「把钱打扮成一项生意」义。

items.en: Investment then named the sum, the act, and the assets.
items.cn: investment 由此兼指金额、行为与资产。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- stem; the near-meaning group holds money words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 词干；近义组收金融相关的词。

entries.definition: The verb of putting money in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」。

entries.definition: The person who puts money in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资者」。

entries.definition: To examine in order to find the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Money provided for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「资金」，多指拨款。

entries.definition: Money used to start or grow a business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「资本」。

entries.definition: Money placed in a bank account.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「存款」，偏储蓄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold on to the image of money dressed up to grow.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「钱换上衣裳去长大」的画面。

normal.en: Invest originally meant to clothe; investment dresses money in a venture.
normal.cn: invest 本义是穿衣；investment 给钱换上生意的衣裳。

normal.en: Return on investment asks whether the new clothes paid off.
normal.cn: return on investment 问的就是这身新衣有没有回本。

normal.en: You can invest money, time, or patience.
normal.cn: 钱、时间、耐心都可以 invest。

normal.en: Foreign investment moves across borders looking for growth.
normal.cn: foreign investment 越过边界寻找增长。

normal.en: Keep it apart from investigate, which follows footprints.
normal.cn: 别和 investigate 混：那个词是顺着脚印查。

abstract.en: Investment is a promise made in the form of money.
abstract.cn: 投资是用钱的形式做出的一句承诺。

abstract.en: Every tree you water is an investment in shade.
abstract.cn: 你浇的每一棵树，都是对荫凉做的投资。

abstract.en: Time is the only investment that cannot be recovered.
abstract.cn: 时间是唯一不可收回的投资。

examples.en: The factory needs foreign investment to expand.
examples.cn: 这家工厂需要外国投资才能扩张。

examples.en: Her years of study were an investment in herself.
examples.cn: 多年的学习是她对自己的投资。

examples.en: He sold his investments before the market fell.
examples.cn: 市场下跌前他卖掉了手上的投资。

dict_mnemonic.text: invest（投入）+ ment（名词）——投进去的那笔东西

root: 拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」→ investire「穿上官袍、授予」→ 英语 invest（投资），加 -ment 成 investment。同族有 invest、investor、investigate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: money put in for gain, the act of putting in, effort given, and the assets held.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：为获利投入的钱、投入行为、付出的心力，以及所持有的资产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of money planted in a pit like a seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠钱像种子一样被埋进土坑。

branches.en: THE BAKERY: a small sum placed in a friend's shop.
branches.cn: 烘焙店这条线：投进朋友店里的小笔钱。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: spending turned into a process.
branches.cn: 机器这条线：被当作过程来看的支出。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE: three years paid into a skill.
branches.cn: 语言这条线：为一项技能付出的三年。

branches.en: THE LAND: the holdings the money now lives in.
branches.cn: 土地这条线：钱如今栖身的那些资产。

branches.en: THE LINK: both trust that today's cost becomes tomorrow's gain.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都相信今天的代价会换来明天的收获。

intro.cn: investment 是 invest 加名词词尾 -ment，源自拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestire and investire are recorded; the money sense is English.

items.exampleCN: 它标出把一物放进另一物。

definition_zh: 看不见的；无形的；不受注意的
definition_en: not able to be seen because it is too small, too far, clear, or simply unnoticed
core_image: 一块玻璃立在空地上，人一走过去就消失在里面
scene: 实验台上一支玻璃管里冒气，肉眼什么都看不出来。The gas is invisible, but it turns the litmus paper blue.
sceneCN: 这里 invisible 是「看不见的」（第 1 个义项：眼睛无法察觉），句意为这种气体看不见，却能让蓝色石蕊试纸变色。画面里的物件：玻璃管、石蕊试纸、手套。

pos.zh: 形容词：看不见的；无形的；不受注意的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「隐形；不可见性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「无形地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看得见的」
同带 vis- 词根的形近词，义为「视力；远见」

senses.title: Cannot be seen
senses.definition: impossible for the eye to notice because of size, distance, or colourlessness
senses.definitionCN: 因为太小、太远或没有颜色而无法被眼睛察觉
senses.example: The bacteria are invisible without a microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 没有显微镜，这些细菌是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre meant "to see"; in- negatives the verb visibilis comes from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看见」，in- 把 visibilis 所自的动词否定掉。

senses.title: Wrongly ignored
senses.definition: present but not noticed or counted by people who should care
senses.definitionCN: 实际存在却被本该关心的人忽略或不算在内
senses.example: Older carers often feel invisible to the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的照护者常觉得在医疗体系里没人看见他们。
senses.why: Social use takes the eye metaphor into institutions: what is not counted is not seen.
senses.whyCN: 社会用法把眼睛的比喻带进制度：没被统计的，就等于没被看见。

senses.title: Not obvious in money or power
senses.definition: hidden in form but real in effect, like costs or forces
senses.definitionCN: 形式上隐藏、实际却有效果，如成本或力量
senses.example: Every purchase carries invisible costs for the river.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次购买都为这条河带来看不见的代价。
senses.why: Accounts talk about invisible balances when the effect is real but the form is not on the page.
senses.whyCN: 账目里的「无形」余额，说的是效果真实、却不写在纸面上。

intro.en: Invisible is Latin in- "not" plus visibilis, "that can be seen", from videre "to see".
intro.cn: invisible 是拉丁 in-「不」加 visibilis「可见的」，后者来自 videre「看」。

items.en: videre meant "to see".
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」。

items.en: visibilis meant "able to be seen".
items.cn: visibilis 意为「能被看见的」。

items.en: in- negated it to invisibilis, "not visible".
items.cn: in- 将其否定为 invisibilis「看不见的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into English forms.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带入英语形式。

items.en: Science and economics borrowed it for gases, germs, and hidden costs.
items.cn: 科学与经济学借它说气体、细菌与隐性成本。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis- root; the near-meaning group holds words for what cannot be noticed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis- 词根；近义组收表示无法察觉的词。

entries.definition: Able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「可见的」，只少否定前缀。

entries.definition: Impossible to defeat.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可战胜的」，拼写只差两个字母。

entries.definition: Related to sight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「视觉的」，同词根。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「隐藏的」，多为有意。

entries.definition: Not noticed by anyone watching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「未被看见的」，偏观察角度。

entries.definition: Real but impossible to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「无形的」，强调摸不着。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word tied to the small prefix that says no.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它系在那个表示「不」的小前缀上。

normal.en: in- says not, and visible says able to be seen.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，visible 是「能被看见」。

normal.en: Glass is visible only by its edge.
normal.cn: 玻璃只有靠边缘才看得出来。

normal.en: Invisible ink has to be warmed to show up.
normal.cn: 隐形墨水要加热才显现。

normal.en: Remove in- and the word turns into its exact opposite.
normal.cn: 去掉 in-，这个词就变成它的正相反。

normal.en: A person can be invisible without vanishing.
normal.cn: 人可以不消失，却「不被看见」。

abstract.en: Invisibility is a matter of who is looking, not only of what is there.
abstract.cn: 无形不只取决于有没有东西，还取决于谁在看。

abstract.en: Some costs never appear on the receipt.
abstract.cn: 有些代价永远不会出现在小票上。

abstract.en: The ignored are the truest invisible ones.
abstract.cn: 被忽略的人，才是最彻底的无形。

examples.en: Ultraviolet light is invisible but burns the skin.
examples.cn: 紫外线看不见，却会晒伤皮肤。

examples.en: The seam was made invisible with tiny stitches.
examples.cn: 那道缝用极细的针脚做成了看不见的。

examples.en: Cleaners work at night and stay invisible to most staff.
examples.cn: 保洁员夜里工作，对大多数员工来说一直「看不见」。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vis（看）+ ible（能……的）——看不到的

root: 拉丁语 in-「不」+ videre「看」→ visibilis「可见的」→ invisibilis → 英语 invisible。同族有 visible、vision、visual、invisibility。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: hidden from the eye, ignored by people, and real but not obvious.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：肉眼看不见、被人忽视，以及真实却不显形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is there, but the eye slides past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：东西就在那里，眼睛却滑过去了。

branches.en: THE GLASS: clear things that show only at the edge.
branches.cn: 玻璃这条线：只在边缘显形的透明物。

branches.en: THE COUNT: people left out of the numbers.
branches.cn: 统计这条线：被数字落下的人。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: forces with real weight and no line on the page.
branches.cn: 账本这条线：真有分量却没有条目的力量。

branches.en: THE EYE: both senses depend on someone failing to notice.
branches.cn: 眼睛这条线：两个义项都取决于有人没留意到。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: institutions decide what becomes visible.
branches.cn: 制度这条线：是制度决定什么能被看见。

intro.en: Invisible is in- "not", vis- "see", and -ible "able to be".
intro.cn: invisible 是 in-「不」、vis-「看」与 -ible「能被……的」三段。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and invisibilis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 invisibilis 均有记载。

items.example: It flips visible into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它把 visible 翻成反义。

items.example: The root also appears in vision and visual.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 vision 与 visual。

items.example: It forms visible, able to be seen.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 visible，能被看见的。

items.example: It forms invisibility.
It forms invisibly.
The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.meaning: sight or a plan seen ahead
items.example: Same root, different ending.
Same root with an adjective ending.

definition_zh: 邀请；招待；招致（麻烦、批评）
definition_en: to ask someone to come somewhere or do something, or to make something likely to happen
core_image: 一扇门被推开，主人朝外伸出手做个「请进」的姿势
scene: 周末的厨房里炖着汤，主人擦擦手，走到门口朝对面的邻居招手。She invited the whole street to dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 invite 是「邀请」（第 1 个义项：请别人来），句意为她请了整条街的人来吃晚饭。画面里的物件：汤锅、门口、手巾。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「邀请；邀请函」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「诱人的」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「被邀请者」
由本词加 -ional 构成，义为「邀请制的」

senses.title: Asking someone to come
senses.definition: to ask a person politely to come to an event or a place
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请人到某个活动或某个地方来
senses.example: They invited us to the wedding in June.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请我们参加六月的婚礼。
senses.why: Latin invitare meant "to ask, to entertain", with no need for a written card.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invitare 意为「邀请、款待」，那时还不需要请柬。

senses.title: Offering hospitality
senses.definition: to receive someone as a guest and provide food or lodging
senses.definitionCN: 把某人当客人接来，并提供饭食或住处
senses.example: A neighbour invited the stranded family in for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居把滞留的那家人请进屋喝茶。
senses.why: The same verb covers the welcome itself, not just the asking.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也涵盖「招待」这件事，而不只是开口请。

senses.title: Bringing trouble on yourself
senses.definition: to make something bad or unwanted more likely by your own action
senses.definitionCN: 因为自己的举动让不好的事情更容易发生
senses.example: Leaving the gate open invites trouble at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里不关院门是会招来麻烦的。
senses.why: The "trouble" sense is the welcoming gesture aimed at something harmful.
senses.whyCN: 「招麻烦」义就是同一个欢迎手势，只是指向了有害的东西。

senses.title: Welcoming a response
senses.definition: to openly welcome comments, questions, or applications
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示乐于接受意见、提问或报名
senses.example: The paper invites readers to send in photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸欢迎读者寄来照片。
senses.why: A request for replies is still an invitation, only written to many at once.
senses.whyCN: 征集回应仍是邀请，只不过一次写给许多人。

intro.en: Invite has kept its original meaning of asking and welcoming almost unchanged for two thousand years.
intro.cn: invite 两千年来几乎原封不动地保留了「邀请、款待」的原意。

items.en: invitare meant "to ask, to treat as a guest".
items.cn: invitare 意为「邀请、当客人款待」。

items.en: The noun invitatus recorded the welcoming of a guest.
items.cn: 名词 invitatus 记载了对客人的接待。

items.en: French had inviter, used for asking someone over.
items.cn: 法语有 inviter，用于请人过来。

items.en: English shortened the French verb to invite.
items.cn: 英语把法语动词缩成 invite。

items.en: The sense of inviting trouble grew from the idea of welcoming.
items.cn: 「招来麻烦」义从「迎接」的想法里长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invi- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for asking people in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invi- 开头；近义组收表示请人进来的词。

entries.definition: A spoken or written request to come.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请；请柬」，同族词。

entries.definition: To put money or effort in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: To make something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: The general verb for requesting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「请；问」，最泛。

entries.definition: To greet someone with pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「欢迎」，强调态度。

entries.definition: To order someone to come.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「传唤」，带命令色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks put the word at a door being held open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在一扇被扶开的门口。

normal.en: The old verb invitare meant to ask and to treat well.
normal.cn: 古动词 invitare 既指邀请，也指好好招待。

normal.en: What arrives in the post is an invitation.
normal.cn: 寄到手里的东西叫 invitation。

normal.en: The person who receives it is the invitee.
normal.cn: 收到邀请的人叫 invitee。

normal.en: Leave a door open and you invite the wind.
normal.cn: 门留着不关，就是把风请进来。

normal.en: Invite a question and you are glad to hear it.
normal.cn: invite questions 就是欢迎别人提问。

abstract.en: Invitation is a door left open on purpose.
abstract.cn: 邀请就是一扇有意留开的门。

abstract.en: Whatever you welcome decides what follows you home.
abstract.cn: 你欢迎什么，什么就跟你回家。

abstract.en: Inviting trouble is the same gesture, aimed badly.
abstract.cn: 招麻烦是同一个手势，只是指错了方向。

examples.en: She invited two former students back to speak at the school.
examples.cn: 她请了两位往届学生回校演讲。

examples.en: The narrow path invites people to walk faster than they should.
examples.cn: 这条窄路会引诱人走得比该有的速度快。

examples.en: The magazine invites letters from readers of any age.
examples.cn: 这本杂志欢迎任何年龄的读者来信。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进来）+ vite（拉丁 invitare 邀请）——请你进来

root: 拉丁语 invitare「邀请；款待」→ 古法语 inviter → 英语 invite。同族有 invitation、invitee、inviting。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: asking someone over, receiving a guest, drawing trouble, and welcoming replies.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：请人来、招待客人、招来麻烦，以及欢迎回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门开时伸出的那只手。

branches.en: THE CARD: a written or spoken request to come.
branches.cn: 请柬这条线：写出来或说出口的请。

branches.en: THE TABLE: food and shelter given to a guest.
branches.cn: 饭桌这条线：给客人的饭食与住处。

branches.en: THE GATE: an open entry that lets trouble in.
branches.cn: 院门这条线：留开的通道把麻烦放进来。

branches.en: THE OPENNESS: both senses come from a willing yes.
branches.cn: 敞开这条线：两个义项都源于一个乐意的「好」。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what you welcome decides what arrives.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：你欢迎什么，就决定什么到来。

intro.en: Invite keeps a single Latin stem, invit-, plus the verb ending -e.
intro.cn: invite 由一个拉丁词干 invit- 加动词尾 -e 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin invitare and invitatus are both recorded with the friendly sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invitare 与 invitatus 均有记载，都带友好的意味。

items.example: It marks bringing someone in.
The root survives in invite and invitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 invite 与 invitation。

items.example: It forms invitation.
It forms invitee.
It forms the adjective inviting.
The verb is the direct source.
The participle shows the noun form.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词显示名词形式。

items.example: It names the request itself.

definition_zh: 发票；货物清单；开具发票
definition_en: a document that lists goods or services supplied and states the money owed for them
core_image: 一张写清货品与价钱的单据，随货一起递到买方手上
scene: 货已送到，卖方把一张写清数量与价钱的单据交给买方，约定期末付款。The seller sent an invoice with the goods and asked for payment within thirty days.
sceneCN: 这里 invoice 是「发票」（第 1 个义项：列明货物或服务与应付金额的单据）；句意：卖方随货寄出发票，要求三十天内付款。

derivatives.zh: 开票；开票业务：invoice + -ing（动作或业务名词化）
已开票的：invoice + -ed（表示已完成的过去分词后缀）

senses.title: A bill for goods or services supplied
senses.definition: a document that lists goods or services supplied and states the sum to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 列明所供货物或服务并写明应付金额的单据
senses.example: The invoice shows ten boxes at forty pounds each.
senses.exampleCN: 发票上列着十箱货物，每箱四十英镑。
senses.why: Old French envois meant things sent, and the paper that travels with sent goods became the bill.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 envois 意为发送之物，随货同行的单据于是成了账单。

senses.title: A record of a sale kept for tax
senses.definition: a sales document used to record tax and to support a claim for payment
senses.definitionCN: 用于记录税款并作为付款请求凭据的销售单据
senses.example: Keep every invoice for six years for the tax office.
senses.exampleCN: 每张发票都要保存六年，以备税务部门查验。
senses.why: Because the paper proves that a sale took place, it also serves tax accounting.
senses.whyCN: 这张纸证明交易确实发生，因此也服务于税务记账。

senses.title: The amount named on the bill
senses.definition: the sum of money written on a bill, treated as a debt owed
senses.definitionCN: 账单上写明的金额，被视为应付的欠款
senses.example: The invoice for the repairs came to two thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费发票的金额达到两千英镑。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the paper stand for the debt that it records.
senses.whyCN: 借代让这张纸代表它所记录的欠款。

senses.title: To send a bill to a customer
senses.definition: to send a bill to a customer for goods or services supplied
senses.definitionCN: 就所供货物或服务向客户寄送账单
senses.example: We invoice clients at the end of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在每月末给客户开票。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, meaning to do what one does with an invoice.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示做与发票相关的事。

senses.title: A list of goods for customs
senses.definition: a detailed list of goods shipped, used by customs or carriers
senses.definitionCN: 随货列明货物细目的清单，供海关或承运人使用
senses.example: The customs invoice lists each item and its value.
senses.exampleCN: 报关发票逐项列明货物及其价值。
senses.why: The word began as a list of things sent, so the shipping-list sense survives in trade.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指发送之物的清单，因此货运清单义在贸易中保留下来。

senses.title: A digital bill issued by a system
senses.definition: a digital bill sent through a network and recorded in a system
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络发送并记入系统的数字账单
senses.example: The platform issues an electronic invoice the moment the order is paid.
senses.exampleCN: 订单一付款，平台就开具电子发票。
senses.why: The document moved online, and the old name moved with it.
senses.whyCN: 单据搬到线上，旧名称也随之搬了过去。

intro.en: Invoice comes from French envois, things sent, from en voie, on the way, and ultimately from Latin via, a road.
intro.cn: invoice 来自法语 envois（发送之物），出自 en voie（在途中），最终可溯至拉丁语 via（道路）。

items.en: Via means a way or a road.
items.cn: 拉丁语 via 意为道路、路途。

items.en: En voie means on the way, and envoyer means to send.
items.cn: 古法语 en voie 意为在途中，envoyer 意为发送。

items.en: Envois, literally things sent, names a shipment and the list that goes with it.
items.cn: 古法语 envois 字面为发送之物，指一批货物及随货清单。

items.en: Invoice enters English as a list of goods shipped.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 invoice 指随货运送的货物清单。

items.en: The list of goods becomes the bill for them, and tax rules fix its form.
items.cn: 现代英语中货物清单转为账单，税务规则又固定了它的格式。

items.en: Electronic invoicing keeps the old name for a digital document.
items.cn: 现代英语中电子开票让这个旧名沿用为数字单据。

note.en: Invoice looks like a prefixed word but is really a French noun for things sent, and it sits beside billing and payment words.
note.cn: invoice 看起来像带前缀的词，实际是法语中表示发送之物的名词，并与开票、付款类词相邻。

entries.definition: the sound a person makes when speaking
entries.definitionCN: 嗓音；说话声（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: billed; recorded on an invoice
entries.definitionCN: 已开票的（invoice 的过去分词）

entries.definition: a sending, or a closing stanza of a poem
entries.definitionCN: 发送；诗末的跋诗（与 invoice 同出 envois）

entries.definition: a statement of money owed for goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 账单；应付货款清单

entries.definition: a written proof that payment has been made
entries.definitionCN: 收据（证明已经付款，与发票相对）

entries.definition: a summary of amounts due or paid over a period
entries.definitionCN: 对账单；结算单

normalIntro.en: Invoice is a paper that travels with goods: the French source means things sent, so the word carries movement inside it.
normalIntro.cn: invoice 是一张随货同行的纸：法语来源意为发送之物，所以这个词本身就带着「运送」的动感。

normal.en: Invoice and envois share the idea of something sent.
normal.cn: invoice 与 envois 共享「被发送之物」这一意思。

normal.en: The invoice travels with the goods, which is why the word once meant the shipping list.
normal.cn: 发票随货同行，所以这个词曾经指货运清单。

normal.en: Compare bill and invoice: a bill is everyday, an invoice is the commercial record.
normal.cn: 对比 bill 与 invoice：bill 更日常，invoice 是商业记录。

normal.en: Invoicing is the process; an invoice is the paper or the file.
normal.cn: invoicing 是流程，invoice 是那张纸或那个文件。

normal.en: A tax invoice must carry a number, a date, and the amount of tax.
normal.cn: 税务发票必须载明号码、日期与税额。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper riding on top of a crate as it leaves the warehouse.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸贴在木箱顶上，随箱子离开仓库。

abstract.en: See a clerk open a folder of numbered sheets so that every sale can be proved.
abstract.cn: 想象职员打开一册编了号的单据，让每笔销售都能被证明。

abstract.en: Think of the total at the foot of the page turning into a debt that must be paid.
abstract.cn: 想象页面底部的合计变成一笔必须偿还的欠款。

examples.en: Please send the invoice to our accounts department.
examples.cn: 请把发票寄给我们的会计部门。

examples.en: The invoice was paid by bank transfer on Friday.
examples.cn: 这张发票已在周五通过银行转账付清。

examples.en: Suppliers invoice the store monthly for the goods delivered.
examples.cn: 供应商每月就所供货物向这家商店开票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因货」——因为发了货才开的单子，就是发票；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 envois（发送之物，出自 en voie「在途中」，可溯至拉丁语 via「道路」）→ 英语 invoice，核心义「随货发送的清单，后转指账单」。

sensesIntro.en: Invoice begins as a list of goods sent, becomes the bill for those goods, then splits into tax record, amount owed, verb use, customs list, and digital bill.
sensesIntro.cn: invoice 最初指发送货物的清单，随后成为这些货物的账单，再分出税务凭证、应付金额、动词用法、报关清单与电子单据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper travelling on top of a crate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸贴在木箱顶上，随货前行。

branches.en: The bill for supplied goods is the everyday commercial sense.
branches.cn: 为所供货物开具的账单，是日常商业义项。

branches.en: Tax rules turn the same paper into an accounting record.
branches.cn: 税务规则把同一张纸变成会计记录。

branches.en: The sum written on the paper stands for the debt it records.
branches.cn: 纸上写明的金额，代表它所记录的欠款。

branches.en: The verb and the digital bill show the document in action and online.
branches.cn: 动词义与电子发票，分别展示这张单据的动作与线上形态。

branches.en: Customs and carriers keep the original shipping-list sense.
branches.cn: 海关与承运人保留了最初的货运清单义。

intro.en: Invoice has no negative prefix: the in- is the tail of French envois, the word for things sent, so the spelling can mislead.
intro.cn: invoice 并没有否定前缀：其中的 in- 是法语 envois（发送之物）的词尾残留，因此拼写容易误导。

latinIntro.en: The French phrase en voie, on the way, goes back to Latin via, a road, which is the oldest layer of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 法语短语 en voie（在途中）可回溯到拉丁语 via（道路），这是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: Latin via is the road behind envoy and invoice.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 via 是 envoy 与 invoice 背后的那条路。

items.example: Goods en voie are still travelling.
Envoyer sends both the goods and the paper.
items.exampleCN: envoyer 既发送货物，也发送单据。

items.example: Envois is the direct source of invoice.
items.exampleCN: envois 是 invoice 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a bill for goods or services
items.example: Invoice keeps the image of goods sent.
items.exampleCN: invoice 保留了货物被发送的意象。

items.example: The invoiced amount must match the order.
items.exampleCN: 已开票的金额必须与订单一致。

items.meaning: the act or business of issuing invoices
items.example: Electronic invoicing replaced the paper book.
items.exampleCN: 电子开票取代了纸质票据簿。

items.example: Voice is only a spelling neighbour of invoice.
items.exampleCN: voice 只是 invoice 的拼写邻居。

items.example: A bill is the everyday word for an invoice.
items.exampleCN: bill 是 invoice 的日常说法。

items.meaning: proof that payment has been made
items.example: A receipt follows an invoice once it is paid.
items.exampleCN: 发票付清之后会有一张收据。

definition_zh: 涉及；包含；使卷入；需要
definition_en: to include someone or something as a necessary part, or to draw a person into an activity or problem
core_image: 一张卷起的纸，把旁边的东西一层层包进去
scene: 事故现场拉着警戒线，几个路过的人也被记录成了证人。The delay involved three separate repairs and two inspections.
sceneCN: 这里 involve 是「涉及」（第 1 个义项：把某事作为组成部分包含在内），句意为这次延误涉及三轮维修和两次检查。画面里的物件：警戒线、记录本、铁皮。

pos.zh: 动词：涉及；包含；使卷入；需要

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「参与；牵连」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「复杂的；有关的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」
同带 volv- 词根的形近词，义为「进化；演变」

senses.title: Having something as a part
senses.definition: to include something as a necessary part of a process or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为过程或情形中必要的一部分包含进来
senses.example: The job involves long hours in cold rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要长时间待在冷库里。
senses.why: involvere rolled things inside; a job that includes a task has rolled the task in.
senses.whyCN: involvere 是把东西卷在里面；一份工作含有某项任务，就是把它卷了进来。

senses.title: Drawing people in
senses.definition: to make someone take part in or be affected by something
senses.definitionCN: 使人参与某事或受到某事影响
senses.example: The decision involved every member of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定牵涉到村里的每一个人。
senses.why: People wrapped into a matter are involved parties, whether they wished it or not.
senses.whyCN: 被卷进一件事的人就是当事方，愿不愿意都一样。

senses.title: Being complicated
senses.definition: to become difficult because many parts are tangled together
senses.definitionCN: 因为许多部分缠在一起而变得难以处理
senses.example: The case grew more involved with each new witness.
senses.exampleCN: 随着新证人出现，这个案子变得越来越复杂。
senses.why: Many threads rolled tight make a knot: that is the complicated sense.
senses.whyCN: 许多线被紧紧卷在一起就成了结，这就是「复杂」那一层。

intro.en: Involve comes from Latin involvere, "to roll up, to wrap", which is literally a paper rolled around something.
intro.cn: involve 来自拉丁语 involvere「卷起、包裹」，字面就是纸把东西卷进去。

items.en: The verb volvere meant "to roll".
items.cn: 动词 volvere 意为「滚、卷」。

items.en: in- added the idea of inward motion, giving involvere, "to roll in".
items.cn: in- 加上向内，构成 involvere「卷进去」。

items.en: The verb was used of wrapping things in cloth or mist.
items.cn: 这个词被用来指用布或雾把东西包起来。

items.en: French took it in as involver, "to wrap up".
items.cn: 法语以 involver「包裹」吸收它。

items.en: The wrapped sense turned into the social sense of being entangled in a matter.
items.cn: 「包住」义转成在社会事务中被缠住的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -volve stem; the near-meaning group holds words for including or entangling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -volve 词干；近义组收表示包含或牵连的词。

entries.definition: To develop gradually over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「演变」，同一词干换前缀。

entries.definition: To turn around a centre.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「旋转」，同词干。

entries.definition: Complicated, or taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「复杂的；有关的」，同族词。

entries.definition: To have something as part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「包括」，最中性。

entries.definition: To make something necessary as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「必然涉及」，偏后果。

entries.definition: To twist into a complicated situation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「缠住」，偏麻烦。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all start with a sheet of paper being rolled up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都从一张被卷起的纸开始。

normal.en: in- means in, and volv- means roll.
normal.cn: in- 是「向内」，volv- 是「卷」。

normal.en: Involve is to roll something into the middle.
normal.cn: involve 就是把东西卷到里面去。

normal.en: What gets rolled in is involved in the affair.
normal.cn: 被卷进去的，就是牵扯其中的。

normal.en: Revolve rolls around an axis; evolve rolls out.
normal.cn: revolve 绕轴卷，evolve 向外卷开。

normal.en: Adding -ment gives the state of involvement.
normal.cn: 加 -ment 就是 involvement 这个状态。

abstract.en: To involve is to fold someone into the story.
abstract.cn: involve 就是把某人褶进这个故事里。

abstract.en: Every wrapped thing has edges you did not plan.
abstract.cn: 每一个被包住的东西都有你没算到的折角。

abstract.en: Complication is many threads rolled tight.
abstract.cn: 复杂就是许多线被紧紧卷在一起。

examples.en: The repair involves replacing the whole pump.
examples.cn: 这次维修要更换整个水泵。

examples.en: Parents were involved in planning the new playground.
examples.cn: 家长参与了新游乐场的筹划。

examples.en: Keep the story simple; the readers do not want an involved plot.
examples.cn: 故事写简单些，读者不想要错综复杂的情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ volve（卷）——被卷进来

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ volvere「卷」→ involvere「卷进去、包裹」→ 古法语 involver → 英语 involve。同族有 involvement、involved；形近 revolve、evolve。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: including a part, drawing people in, and becoming tangled and complex.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：包含组成部分、把人牵进来，以及变得盘根错节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet rolled inward until other things are inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸向内卷起，把别的东西也裹了进去。

branches.en: THE STEPS: what a job or plan must contain.
branches.cn: 步骤这条线：一份工作或计划必须含有的环节。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: everyone rolled into the matter.
branches.cn: 人物这条线：被卷进这件事的所有人。

branches.en: THE KNOT: a case too tangled to explain quickly.
branches.cn: 绳结这条线：复杂到一时说不清的案子。

branches.en: THE WEB: parts and people are bound by the same thread.
branches.cn: 网这条线：组成部分与人被同一根线连着。

branches.en: THE COST: drawing people in is what makes things complicated.
branches.cn: 代价这条线：把人牵进来，事情才变复杂。

intro.en: Involve is in- "into" plus volv- "roll".
intro.cn: involve 是 in-「进入」加 volv-「卷」。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and involvere are both recorded roll-words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 与 involvere 都是有记载的「卷」类词。

items.example: It turns rolling into wrapping.
The root also drives revolve and evolve.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也带动 revolve 与 evolve。

items.example: It forms involvement.
It forms involved, tangled or related.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 involved，纠结或有关的。

items.example: It forms involving, gripping.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 involving，引人入胜的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The re- prefix sends it around.
The e- prefix rolls it outward.
items.exampleCN: e- 前缀把它向外卷开。

definition_zh: 参与；投入；牵连；涉及
definition_en: the state of taking part in something or of being connected with it, often as a matter of responsibility
core_image: 一只手伸进正在运转的机器里，成了它的一部分
scene: 社区中心墙上贴着排班表，好几位老人每周都来分菜。Her involvement in the food bank began with one afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 involvement 是「参与」（第 1 个义项：主动投入某项活动），句意为她在食品银行的参与从某一个下午开始。画面里的物件：排班表、菜筐、记号笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 构成，义为「涉及；使卷入」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「参与的；复杂的」
同以 in- 开头、invol- 词干的形近词，义为「非自愿的」

senses.title: Taking an active part
senses.definition: the fact of actively giving your time or effort to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 主动把时间或精力投入到某项活动中的事实
senses.example: Her involvement in the choir gave her a way to make friends.
senses.exampleCN: 参加合唱团让她找到了交朋友的方式。
senses.why: The -ment noun turns the act of joining in into a lasting relation.
senses.whyCN: -ment 名词把「加入」这个动作变成一种持续的关系。

senses.title: Being connected to a trouble
senses.definition: the state of being linked to an accident, crime, or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 与事故、犯罪或丑闻被联系在一起的状态
senses.example: He denied any involvement in the theft.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认与这起盗窃有任何牵连。
senses.why: Here the wrapping is unwanted: a name rolled into a police file.
senses.whyCN: 这里的包裹是不情愿的：一个名字被卷进了警方的卷宗。

senses.title: Emotional commitment
senses.definition: a deep personal interest or feeling that makes leaving hard
senses.definitionCN: 一种让人难以抽身的深切私人兴趣或情感
senses.example: Her emotional involvement in the case tested her judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个案子的情感投入影响了她的判断。
senses.why: Feeling can be wrapped in too, and that is the heaviest kind of involvement.
senses.whyCN: 情感也会被卷进去，那是最沉的一种投入。

intro.en: Involvement is the noun from involve, which began as Latin involvere, "to wrap".
intro.cn: involvement 是 involve 的名词，而 involve 起初就是拉丁 involvere「包裹」。

items.en: volvere meant "to roll".
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚、卷」。

items.en: involvere meant "to roll in, to wrap".
items.cn: involvere 意为「卷进、包裹」。

items.en: French passed the verb in as involver.
items.cn: 法语以 involver 传入这个动词。

items.en: English added -ment to name the state of being wrapped in.
items.cn: 英语加 -ment 指「被包进去」的状态。

items.en: Modern usage splits the noun into participation and complicity.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个名词分成「参与」与「牵连」两面。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the involv- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用 involv- 词干；近义组收表示参与的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to include or entangle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「涉及；卷入」，同族词。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相近。

entries.definition: Done without a choice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「非自愿的」，同前缀。

entries.definition: The act of taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「参与」，最直接的对等词。

entries.definition: A promise and the effort to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投入；承诺」。

entries.definition: Involvement in wrongdoing with others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「同谋」，只用于坏事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the noun back to a rolled-up sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个名词系回一张卷好的纸。

normal.en: It is involve plus -ment, the state itself.
normal.cn: 它是 involve 加 -ment，指那个状态本身。

normal.en: You roll into an activity: that is involvement.
normal.cn: 你把自己卷进一项活动，这就是参与。

normal.en: You can roll into trouble just as easily.
normal.cn: 同样容易把自己卷进麻烦里。

normal.en: The -ment turns the act into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: -ment 把动作变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Denying involvement is a sentence you hear after scandals.
normal.cn: 丑闻之后总能听到「否认牵连」这句话。

abstract.en: Involvement is the footprint of an interest.
abstract.cn: 参与就是兴趣留下的脚印。

abstract.en: Being inside is warmth and also weight.
abstract.cn: 身在其中，既是温度也是重量。

abstract.en: Once wrapped in, you never unwrap completely.
abstract.cn: 一旦被卷进来，就很难完全卷出去。

examples.en: The school credits its success to parent involvement.
examples.cn: 学校把成功归功于家长的参与。

examples.en: The report found no involvement of local officials.
examples.cn: 报告认定没有当地官员牵涉其中。

examples.en: Her deep involvement with the study left little time for sleep.
examples.cn: 她对这个研究投入极深，几乎没时间睡觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: involve（卷入）+ ment（状态）——被卷进去的那种状态

root: 拉丁语 involvere「卷进去」→ involve → 加 -ment 成 involvement。同族有 involve、involved；形近 investment、involuntary。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: active part, connection to trouble, and emotional commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：主动参与、与麻烦的牵连，以及感情上的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into a running machine and staying there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进运转的机器并留在里面。

branches.en: THE ROTA: hours written on a board and given away.
branches.cn: 排班表这条线：写在板上、交付出去的时间。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a name placed at a scene of trouble.
branches.cn: 记录这条线：名字被放到出事的地方。

branches.en: THE HEART: a case that will not let go of you.
branches.cn: 心这条线：一个放不下手的案子。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses are a tie between person and event.
branches.cn: 关联这条线：两个义项都是人与事件的连带。

branches.en: THE COST: what you give yourself to takes something back.
branches.cn: 代价这条线：你付出给的事也会取走些什么。

intro.en: Involvement is in- "into", volv- "roll", and -ment naming the state.
intro.cn: involvement 是 in-「进入」、volv-「卷」与标出状态的 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Latin volvere and involvere, both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族立足的拉丁语 volvere 与 involvere 均有记载。

items.example: It marks being put inside.
The root also drives revolve.
It forms involvement.
It forms the adjective involved.
It forms involuntary.
The verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的后盾。

items.example: The simplest member of the family.
A cousin that keeps the rolling image.

definition_zh: 内心的；向内的；内部的
definition_en: directed towards the inside of something, or happening privately in the mind
core_image: 一支箭头从外面折回，指向自己胸口的方向
scene: 车窗外的城市飞速后退，他不再看风景，目光落在膝盖上的旧照片。A long train ride always turns him inward.
sceneCN: 这里 inward 是「向内、转向内心」（第 2 个义项：注意力回到自己心里），句意为长途坐火车总让他转向内心。画面里的物件：车窗、旧照片、膝上的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：内心的；向内的；内部的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「向内地」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内心」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「内在性」
同构的相反词，义为「向外的」

senses.title: Pointing to the inside
senses.definition: facing or moving towards the centre of something
senses.definitionCN: 朝向或移向某物的中心
senses.example: The door opens with an inward swing.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门是向内开的。
senses.why: The suffix -weard marks the direction of a turn, as in forward.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -weard 标出转身的方向，正如 forward。

senses.title: Turned to the mind
senses.definition: directed at your own thoughts and feelings rather than at the world outside
senses.definitionCN: 指向自己内心的想法与感受，而非外部世界
senses.example: Her inward life was far busier than her quiet days suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 她的内心生活远比表面安静的日子忙碌。
senses.why: The same arrow was turned from rooms to feelings by later writers.
senses.whyCN: 后世的写作者把同一支箭头从房间转向了感受。

senses.title: Inside a body or building
senses.definition: situated on the inside part of a body or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于身体或建筑结构内侧的
senses.example: The inward wall was damp after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，内墙是潮的。
senses.why: In building and anatomy the word stays physical and means the inner face.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑与解剖里这个词仍指实物，意为内侧的那一面。

intro.en: Inward is a native English compound: the preposition in plus the old suffix -weard, "turned towards".
intro.cn: inward 是英语本土的复合词：介词 in 加上古词尾 -weard「朝向」。

items.en: The word innan meant "within".
items.cn: 古英语 innan 意为「在里面」。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant "turned towards", as in toward.
items.cn: 词尾 -weard 意为「朝向」，与 toward 同源。

items.en: inweard joined them: turned towards the inside.
items.cn: inweard 把两者合起：朝向内的一面。

items.en: Middle English kept inward for the body and the spirit alike.
items.cn: 中古英语用 inward 兼指身体与心灵。

items.en: Modern English added the -ly adverb to mark the mental sense.
items.cn: 现代英语加 -ly 副词来标出心理义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ward direction suffix; the near-meaning group holds words for the inner world.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ward 方向词尾；近义组收表示内在世界的词。

entries.definition: Turned towards the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「向外的」，镜像词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, moving to the inside.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「向内」，同族词。

entries.definition: The one nearer the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，强调位置。

entries.definition: Happening inside a thing or body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，偏客观。

entries.definition: Kept to oneself, not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「私人的」，偏不公开。

entries.definition: Habitually looking into one's own mind.

definition_zh: 离子；带电荷的原子或原子团
definition_en: an atom or group of atoms that carries an electric charge
core_image: 一个原子失去一个电子后，周围浮起加号，被另一侧的减号吸过去
scene: 一个原子失去一个电子后，周围浮起加号，被另一侧的减号吸过去。Each ion in the solution carries either a positive or a negative charge.
sceneCN: 这里 ion 指带电荷的原子或原子团（第 1 个义项：因得到或失去电子而带电的粒子）；句意：溶液中的每个离子都带正电或负电。图中可辨识物件：原子核、散去的电子、加号、另一侧的减号。

senses.title: A charged atom or group
senses.titleCN: 带电荷的原子或原子团
senses.definition: an atom or group of atoms that has gained or lost electrons and therefore carries a charge
senses.definitionCN: 因得到或失去电子而带有电荷的原子或原子团
senses.example: Each ion in the solution carries either a positive or a negative charge.
senses.exampleCN: 溶液中的每个离子都带正电或负电。
senses.why: Faraday took a Greek participle meaning a going thing and applied it to the particles that travel through a solution to the electrodes.
senses.whyCN: 法拉第取用一个意为「正在走的东西」的希腊分词，用来指在溶液中游向电极的粒子。

senses.title: A positive ion
senses.definition: an ion that has lost electrons and carries a net positive charge, also called a cation
senses.definitionCN: 失去电子、带净正电荷的离子，也称阳离子
senses.example: A positive ion moves toward the negative electrode.
senses.exampleCN: 正离子朝阳极移动。
senses.why: charge has two signs, so the general word splits at once into positive and negative cases.
senses.whyCN: 电荷只有两种符号，因此通称立刻分成正、负两种情形。

senses.title: A negative ion
senses.definition: an ion that has gained electrons and carries a net negative charge, also called an anion
senses.definitionCN: 得到电子、带净负电荷的离子，也称阴离子
senses.example: A negative ion is attracted to the positive plate.
senses.exampleCN: 负离子被正极板吸引。
senses.why: the other sign of charge needs its own label, and English uses the same noun with an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 另一种电荷符号需要自己的标签，英语就用同一个名词加形容词来表示。

senses.title: A freely moving ion in solution
senses.titleCN: 溶液中自由移动的离子
senses.definition: an ion dissolved in a liquid, free to move and therefore able to carry current
senses.definitionCN: 溶于液体、可自由移动、因而能载流的离子
senses.example: The ions in seawater let it conduct electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 海水中的离子使它能够导电。
senses.why: the word's first sense was exactly this mobile particle, and solution chemistry kept it as the everyday meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初的义项正是这种会移动的粒子，溶液化学把它保留为日常含义。

senses.title: An ion in a plasma
senses.definition: a charged particle in a gas hot enough to be partly ionised
senses.definitionCN: 在热到部分电离的气体中存在的带电粒子
senses.example: The ions and electrons in the plasma drift along the magnetic field.
senses.exampleCN: 等离子体中的离子与电子沿磁场漂移。
senses.why: when a whole gas becomes charged, the same noun names its charged component beside the electrons.
senses.whyCN: 当整团气体带电时，同一个名词指其带电成分，与电子并列。

senses.title: An ion in physiology
senses.definition: a charged atom such as sodium or potassium that carries signals across cell membranes
senses.definitionCN: 如钠、钾等带电原子，跨细胞膜传递信号
senses.example: Calcium ions trigger the muscle to contract.
senses.exampleCN: 钙离子触发肌肉收缩。
senses.why: biology speaks of ions whenever a charged atom, not an electron, does the work of signalling.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，只要执行信号功能的是带电原子而非电子，就用「离子」这个词。

senses.title: An ion in beams and implantation
senses.titleCN: 离子束与离子注入中的离子
senses.definition: a charged atom accelerated in a beam for analysis, etching or doping a material
senses.definitionCN: 在束流中被加速，用于分析、刻蚀或掺杂材料的带电原子
senses.example: The instrument fires ions at the surface to measure its layers.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器向表面发射离子，以测量其各层。
senses.why: industry and analysis turn the particle into a tool, and the noun survives unchanged in the fixed phrases.
senses.whyCN: 工业与分析把这种粒子变成工具，名词在固定说法中原样保留。

senses.title: An ion in space propulsion
senses.definition: a charged atom accelerated electrically to produce thrust in an ion engine
senses.definitionCN: 在离子发动机中被电加速以产生推力的带电原子
senses.example: The probe's engine accelerates ions to very high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器的发动机把离子加速到极高速度。
senses.why: spacecraft engineering borrowed the noun for the exhaust of a thruster, since the exhaust really is a stream of ions.
senses.whyCN: 航天工程借这个名词指推进器的尾流，因为尾流确实是一束离子。

intro.en: Ion was coined by Michael Faraday in 1834 from Greek ion, the neuter present participle of ienai, to go. It reached English through scientific Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ion 由法拉第在 1834 年依据希腊语 ion 造出，后者是 ienai「去」的中性现在分词。这个词经科学拉丁语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ienai meant to go or come, and its forms supplied several Greek words of motion. The deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructions.
items.cn: ienai 意为「去、来」，其各种形式提供了若干表示运动的希腊词。更早的印欧语联系属于重构。

items.en: The neuter participle ion meant a going thing, used in Greek of that which moves or travels.
items.cn: 中性分词 ion 意为「正在走的东西」，在希腊语中用于指移动或行进之物。

items.en: Faraday needed a name for the particles that leave the electrodes during electrolysis, and chose the Greek participle, giving English ion.
items.cn: 法拉第需要给电解时离开电极的粒子一个名字，他选了那个希腊分词，于是有了英语 ion。

items.en: Scientific Latin took the word as ion, iontis, and the derived adjective ionicus; the English adjective ionic followed.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语以 ion、iontis 的形式接收这个词，并造出形容词 ionicus；英语形容词 ionic 随后出现。

items.en: Faraday also coined anion and cation from Greek ana-, up, and kata-, down, because of the direction each kind travels.
items.cn: 法拉第还依据希腊语 ana-「向上」与 kata-「向下」，造出 anion 与 cation，因为两类离子的移动方向不同。

items.en: First date uncertain: Faraday's coinage is dated 1834 in his published papers, but the first appearance in an English text is not exactly settled.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：法拉第的造词在其发表论文中记为 1834 年，但它在英语文本中的首次出现没有完全定论。

note.en: The first group is the ion family and its charged subtypes; the second group is the neutral particles and the general word for charge carriers they are often compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是 ion 词族及其带电子类；第二组是中性粒子，以及常与之比较的载流子通称。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of ions; it describes bonds and compounds, and cannot stand as the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「离子的」的形容词；描述键与化合物，不能充当名词本身。

entries.definition: To strip or add electrons so that a neutral particle becomes an ion.
entries.definitionCN: 剥离或添加电子，使中性粒子成为离子。

entries.definition: The process of producing ions; it is the event, not the particle.
entries.definitionCN: 产生离子的过程；是事件，不是粒子。

entries.definition: The negative ion, built with ana-, up, because it rises toward the anode in early electrolysis setups.
entries.definitionCN: 带负电的离子，由 ana-「向上」构成，因为它在早期电解装置中朝阳极上升。

entries.definition: The positive ion, built with kata-, down, the counterpart of anion in the same naming scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 带正电的离子，由 kata-「向下」构成，是同一命名体系中 anion 的对应项。

entries.definition: The neutral particle; an ion is an atom or group that has gained or lost electrons.
entries.definitionCN: 指中性粒子；离子则是得到或失去电子的原子或原子团。

entries.definition: A neutral group of bonded atoms; a charged group of atoms is a molecular ion, not simply a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 由键连接的中性原子团；带电的原子团是分子离子，而不只是分子。

entries.definition: A species with an unpaired electron; it may be neutral or charged, so it overlaps with ion without matching it.
entries.definitionCN: 带未成对电子的物种，可能中性也可能带电，因此与离子有交集但并不等同。

entries.definition: Any particle that carries current, electrons or ions alike; ion names one kind of carrier.
entries.definitionCN: 任何载流粒子，电子或离子皆可；ion 只命名其中一种载流子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek participle, Faraday's date and the real laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊分词、法拉第的年份与真实的实验室说法。

normal.en: Ion is a going thing: the particle that walks to the electrode.
normal.cn: ion 是「正在走的东西」：走向电极的那个粒子。

normal.en: The family runs ion, ionic, ionize, ionization, anion and cation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ion、ionic、ionize、ionization、anion 与 cation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: ion channel, ion beam, ion exchange.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：离子通道、离子束、离子交换。

normal.en: Anion and cation are twins made in the same year by the same man: up and down.
normal.cn: anion 与 cation 是同年由同一人造出的一对：向上与向下。

normal.en: An ion differs from an atom only by electrons, which is why the charge sign is the whole story.
normal.cn: 离子与原子只差电子，所以电荷符号就是全部关键。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller who has lost a bag and now walks faster toward the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一位丢了包的旅客，如今更快地走向登机口。

abstract.en: Picture two queues moving in opposite directions between the same two doors.
abstract.cn: 想象两列人在同两扇门之间朝相反方向移动。

abstract.en: Picture a current in water that is made of particles, not of wire.
abstract.cn: 想象水里的一股电流，由粒子而不是导线构成。

examples.en: The salt splits into ions as soon as it enters the water.
examples.cn: 盐一进入水中就分成离子。

examples.en: A lithium ion battery stores charge by moving ions between layers.
examples.cn: 锂离子电池靠离子在层间移动来储电。

examples.en: The detector counts each ion that passes through the slit.
examples.cn: 探测器统计每一个穿过狭缝的离子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ion」听似「爱用」——爱用电的那颗粒子，带电的原子 → 离子

root: 希腊 ienai「去」→ 中性现在分词 ion「正在走的东西」→ 法拉第 1834 年用作 ion「离子」→ 加 -ic 成 ionic；anion、cation 同出这一命名体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one particle: something charged is on the move. The particle then splits by sign, appears in solution and in plasma, signals inside a body, and finally becomes a tool in beams and in space propulsion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个粒子展开：一个带电之物正在移动。这个粒子随后按符号分正负，出现在溶液与等离子体中，在体内传递信号，最后成为束流与航天推进中的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an atom that has lost an electron, a plus sign floating where the electron was, pulled toward a minus sign across the gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个失去电子的原子，电子原处浮起加号，被对面的减号隔空吸过去。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: an atom or group that gained or lost electrons.
branches.cn: 粒子：得到或失去电子的原子或原子团。

branches.en: TWO SIGNS: the same noun with a plus or a minus attached.
branches.cn: 两种符号：同一个名词配上加号或减号。

branches.en: WHERE IT MOVES: dissolved in liquid, or drifting in an ionised gas.
branches.cn: 在哪里移动：溶于液体，或在电离气体中漂移。

branches.en: THE BODY'S SIGNAL: calcium and sodium ions doing the work of nerves.
branches.cn: 体内的信号：钙与钠离子承担神经的工作。

branches.en: THE TOOL: a beam aimed at a surface, or exhaust pushed out of an engine.
branches.cn: 工具：射向表面的束流，或从发动机喷出的尾流。

intro.en: Ion is one Greek participle that became a scientific noun; its family is built with Greek prefixes and English endings.
intro.cn: ion 是一个变成科学名词的希腊分词；它的词族由希腊前缀与英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin received ion as a Greek loan and added the adjective ionicus; the Latin entries below are borrowings, not native Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把 ion 作为希腊借词接收，并加上形容词 ionicus；下面的拉丁词条是借词，而非拉丁本土词。

items.example: The verb is the source of the participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是那个分词的来源。

items.structure: ion (Greek present participle, a going thing)
items.example: Faraday gave the participle a chemical job.
items.exampleCN: 法拉第给这个分词一份化学职务。

items.structure: the English noun, from the Greek participle
items.example: Every ion carries a charge.
Ionic bonds hold the crystal together.
items.exampleCN: 离子键把晶体维系在一起。

items.example: Radiation can ionize the gas.
Ionization rises with temperature.
items.exampleCN: 电离随温度升高而增加。

items.example: An anion climbs toward the anode.
A cation sinks toward the cathode.
Radio waves bounce off the ionosphere.
items.exampleCN: 无线电波从电离层反射。

items.example: An ion beam can etch a surface layer by layer.
items.exampleCN: 离子束能一层层刻蚀表面。
